When the Day of Resurrection comes, the wicked will be distinguished from the good, the wicked will be piled one upon another, then cast together with its people into Hell. No good person enters the Fire, and no wicked person enters Paradise.

Among them is the desolation that Allah, glorified and exalted, places in the heart of the fornicator, which is the counterpart of the desolation that overspreads his face. The chaste person has sweetness on his face and tranquility in his heart, and whoever sits with him feels at ease with him; but the fornicator has desolation overspreading his face, and whoever sits with him feels estranged from him. Among them is the loss of the awe that is removed from the hearts of his family, his companions and others toward him, and he becomes the most contemptible thing in their souls and eyes, unlike the chaste person, who is granted awe and sweetness. Among them is that people look at him with the eye of treachery, and no one trusts him with his womenfolk or with his children. Among them is the odor that spreads from him, which every person of sound heart smells, emanating from his mouth and body. Were it not that people share this odor, it would waft from its bearer and call out against him, but as it is said:

"Everyone has what I have, except that they are, among some of them toward others, blamers."

Among them is constriction and tightness of the chest, for fornicators are treated contrary to their intentions. Whoever seeks the pleasure and goodness of life through what Allah has forbidden him is punished with the opposite of his aim, for what is with Allah is not attained except through obedience to Him, and Allah has never made disobedience a means to any good. If the sinner knew what there is in chastity of pleasure, joy, expansion of the chest and goodness of life, he would see that what he missed of pleasure is many times over what he obtained, to say nothing of the profit of the outcome and the attainment of Allah's reward and honor. Among them is that he exposes himself to missing the enjoyment of the dark-eyed maidens (hur 'in) in pleasant dwellings in the Gardens of Eden. It has already been mentioned that when Allah, glorified and exalted, punishes one who wears silk in this world by depriving him of wearing it in the Hereafter, and one who drinks wine in this world by depriving him of it in the Hereafter, then likewise one who enjoys forbidden images in this world. Indeed, whatever the servant attains in this world: if he expands in what is lawful, his share on the Day of Resurrection is narrowed by the same measure as he expanded in it; and if he attains something unlawful, he misses its counterpart on the Day of Resurrection.

Among them is that fornication emboldens him to sever family ties, to disobey his parents, to earn unlawful wealth, to wrong people, to neglect his family and dependents, and perhaps leads him forcibly to shed forbidden blood, and perhaps he seeks its help through sorcery and polytheism, knowingly or unknowingly. This sin is not completed except with types of sins before it and with it, and there issue from it other kinds of sins after it. It is surrounded by an army of sins before it and an army after it. It is the thing most conducive to the evils of this world and the Hereafter, and the thing most preventive of the good of this world and the Hereafter. When it fastens upon a servant and he falls into its snares and nets, it becomes hard for the advisers to rescue him, and physicians are baffled by its cure. Its captive is not ransomed, and its slain is not compensated. Allah, glorified, has entrusted it with the removal of blessings. So if a servant is afflicted with it, let him bid farewell to Allah's blessings, for they are a guest that moves quickly and a passing thing that will soon vanish. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿That is because Allah would never change a blessing He had bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves, and indeed Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when Allah intends for a people an ill, there is no repelling it, and they have not besides Him any patron﴾.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 17, verse 36:

If the servant is held accountable and questioned for everything, even for his hearing, his sight, and his heart, as Allah the Most High says: ﴿Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — about all of those one will be questioned﴾ [al-Isra: 36].

So he is worthy of taking account of himself before he is called to account.

The obligation of self-reckoning (muhasabat al-nafs) is also indicated by the words of Allah the Most High: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah. And let every soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow﴾ [al-Hashr: 18].

(Section: Placing hearing before sight)

Hearing (al-sam') precedes sight (al-basar) wherever they occur in the Noble Qur'an, whether as a verbal noun, a verb, or a noun. The first, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — about all of those one will be questioned﴾

The second, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see﴾

The third, as in His saying: ﴿All-Hearing, All-Seeing﴾, ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾, ﴿And Allah was ever All-Hearing, All-Seeing﴾

By this, those who say that hearing is more noble than sight argue, and this is the view of the majority. It is what the companions of al-Shafi'i mentioned, and they, and others, reported from the companions of Abu Hanifa that they said sight is superior. They set up the dispute between them and cited the proofs from both sides. I do not know what rulings depend on this question such that it should be mentioned in the books of jurisprudence. Likewise, the two opinions of the theologians (al-mutakallimun) and the exegetes (al-mufassirun).

Abu al-Ma'ali related from Ibn Qutaybah the preference of sight, and he refuted it. Those who prefer hearing argued that Allah precedes it in the Qur'an wherever they occur, and that through hearing one attains the happiness of this world and the Hereafter, for happiness in its entirety lies in obeying the messengers and believing in what they brought, and this is only grasped through hearing. For this reason, in the hadith narrated by Ahmad and others, from the hadith of al-Aswad ibn Sari', there is: "Three will argue before Allah on the Day of Resurrection..." and he mentioned among them a deaf man who says, "O Lord, Islam came, and I did not hear anything." They also argued that the knowledge acquired through hearing is many times greater than the knowledge acquired through sight, for sight perceives only some of the existing things that are visible and near, while hearing perceives existing things, non-existing things, the present and the absent, the near and the distant, the necessary, the possible, and the impossible. So there is no comparison between the perception of sight and its perception. They also argued that the loss of hearing causes defect in the heart and the tongue, which is why the one deaf from birth generally does not speak. As for the loss of sight, it may sometimes aid the strength of insight's perception and the sharpness of its intelligence, for the light of sight is reflected inwardly into insight, strengthening its perception and magnifying it. For this reason you find many blind people, or most of them, possessing a blazing intelligence, acuteness, and an illumination of the inner sense that you rarely find in a seeing person. There is no doubt that the wandering of sight through regions and lands, and its direct contact with the visible things in their variety, causes the heart to be scattered and dispersed, which is why the night is more gathering for the heart and seclusion is more helpful in hitting upon thought. They said: the deficiency of one who lacks hearing is not like the deficiency of one who lacks sight. For this reason, among the scholars, the virtuous ones, and the imams of Islam there are many who were blind, yet no one is known among them to have been deaf; indeed, no deaf person is known among the Companions. This and similar arguments of theirs for preferring sight were answered by their opponents, who said: two matters will decide between us and you. The first is that what sight perceives is the gazing upon the Face of Allah in the Hereafter, which is the greatest bliss of the people of Paradise and the dearest to them, and nothing is more perfect than the One who is looked upon, glory be to Him; so there is no faculty in the servant more perfect than the faculty by which he sees Him. The second is that this bliss and this gift were attained only through hearing, so hearing was like a means to this supreme goal, and preferring it over the means is like the preference of ends over their means.

As for what you mentioned of the breadth and comprehensiveness of its perceptions, it is countered by the frequency of error in them and the occurrence of mistake, for the correct in what hearing perceives, relative to the abundance of things heard, is little within much; and against the abundance of its perceptions stands the soundness of the perceptions of sight and the absence of deception, and that what one sees and witnesses is not subject to falsehood in the way that what one hears is. When the two ranks are set against each other, the preference remains with what we have mentioned.

Shaykh al-Islam Taqi al-Din Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah sanctify his spirit and illuminate his tomb, said:

"The decisive word is that the perception of hearing is more general and comprehensive, and the perception of sight is more complete and perfect. So this has completeness and perfection, and that has generality and comprehensiveness. Thus each of them is preferred over the other by what is specific to it." End of his words.

And it has been reported in the well-known hadith that the Prophet ﷺ said to Abu Bakr and Umar: "These two are the hearing and the sight." It is sound according to the more likely view. This may bear four interpretations. The first: that the meaning is that they are to me in the position of hearing and sight. The second: that they are, in the religion of Islam, in the position of hearing and sight in a human being, so the Messenger is in the position of the heart and the spirit, and the two of them are in the position of hearing and sight in the religion. On this, there are two possibilities: the first is distribution, so one of them is in the position of hearing and the other in the position of sight; the second is sharing, so that this likening to the two senses holds for each of them, and each of them is in the position of hearing and sight. On the possibility of distribution and division, people disputed which of them is hearing and which is sight, and they built this on which of the two qualities is more excellent. The verification is that the quality of sight belongs to al-Siddiq (Abu Bakr), and the quality of hearing belongs to al-Faruq (Umar). This becomes clear to you from the fact that Umar was a muhaddath, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "There were among the nations before you muhaddathun (those spoken to by inspiration); if there is any in this Ummah, it is Umar."

Narrated by Muslim.

The tahdith mentioned is what is cast into the heart of truth and right, and its path is the inner hearing; it is in the position of tahdith and information in the ear. As for al-Siddiq, he is the one who perfected the station of siddiqiyyah (truthfulness) through the perfection of his insight, so that it is as if his sight had come into direct contact with what the Messenger reported, just as his heart had, so there remained between him and the perception of sight only the veil of the unseen. He is as if he looks upon what he was told of the unseen from behind its curtains. This is due to the perfection of insight, and it is the most excellent of the servant's gifts and the greatest of his honours with which he is honoured; beyond the rank of prophethood there is nothing but it. For this reason, Allah, glory be to Him, placed it after prophethood, saying: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger — those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour: of the prophets, the truthful (al-siddiqin), the martyrs, and the righteous﴾

This is what al-Siddiq preceded others in, not by abundance of fasting nor by abundance of prayer. The possessor of this moves slowly yet arrives first. Whoever has exerted himself toward it, though his journey was not along this path and his striving was not toward this knowledge, has been outstripped by one who strove toward it, even if he crawls crawling and creeps creeping. Do not find this section lengthy, for it is more important than what the speech was aimed at, so return to it.

It is said that placing hearing before sight has two reasons. The first is that the context requires it, such that mentioning them between the two qualities carries a threat and a warning, as the custom of the Qur'an is to threaten and warn the addressees by mentioning His qualities which call for caution and uprightness, such as His saying: ﴿And if you slip after the clear proofs have come to you, then know that Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾

And His saying: ﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world — with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And Allah was ever All-Hearing, All-Seeing﴾

The Noble Qur'an is full of this. On this basis, within it is the meaning: "I hear what they answer you with, and what they confront My messages with, and I see what they do." There is no doubt that those addressed by the message, in regard to response and obedience, are of two kinds: one kind received it with "you have spoken truly" and then acted in accordance with its requirements; the other kind received it with denial and then acted contrary to it. So the rank of what is heard from them comes before the rank of what is seen, and what relates to hearing is placed before what relates to sight. Consider this meaning in His saying to Musa: ﴿Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see﴾

He hears what they answer him with, and sees what they do. This does not encompass all contexts, but is specific to those whose situation is of this kind. The second reason is that denial of corrupt illusions regarding the hearing of speech, despite the great distance between the hearer and the heard, is more severe than denying their seeing despite that distance. In the two Sahihs, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Three men gathered near the House: two Thaqafis and a Qurashi, or two Qurashis and a Thaqafi. One of them said: 'Do you think Allah hears what we say?' The second said: 'He hears if we speak aloud, and does not hear if we conceal.' The third said: 'If He hears when we speak aloud, He hears when we conceal.'" Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, and al-Tirmidhi. They did not say, "Do you think Allah sees us?" So placing hearing first was more important, and the need to know it was more pressing.

A third reason: the movement of the tongue in speech is the greatest of the movements of the limbs and the most powerful in its effect for good and evil, for righteousness and corruption; indeed, most of the actions that come into existence arise after the movement of the tongue. So placing the quality related to it first is more important and more fitting. By this it is known that it is placed before the All-Knowing wherever it occurs.

(Benefit)

Allah, in His wisdom, made every part of the son of Adam, outward and inward, an instrument for something which, when it is used for it, is its perfection. The eye is an instrument for seeing, the ear an instrument for hearing, the nose an instrument for smelling, the tongue an instrument for speech, the private part for marriage, the hand for seizing, the foot for walking, the heart for monotheism and knowledge, the spirit for love, and the intellect is an instrument for reflection and contemplation of the consequences of religious and worldly matters, and for preferring what ought to be preferred and neglecting what ought to be neglected.

The most losing of people in transaction is one who busies himself with himself away from Allah; more losing than him is one who busies himself with people away from himself.

In the Sunan, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id, marfu': "When the son of Adam rises in the morning, all the limbs humble themselves before the tongue, saying: 'Fear Allah regarding us, for we are only by you: if you are upright, we are upright, and if you are crooked, we are crooked.'"

His words "tukfir al-lisan" (humble themselves before the tongue): it is said its meaning is that they submit to it. In the hadith, when the Companions entered upon the Negus, they did not prostrate (lam yakfuru) to him, i.e., they did not prostrate or submit; for this reason 'Amr ibn al-'As said to him: "O King, they do not submit to you, and they only humble themselves to you." The tongue is so called because it is the messenger (bareed) of the heart, its interpreter, and the intermediary between it and the limbs. Their words "innama nahnu bika" (we are only by you): i.e., our salvation is by you and our ruin is by you. For this reason they said: "If you are upright, we are upright, and if you are crooked, we are crooked."

It has been said: [the meaning is] that they would seek a way to Him through overpowering and subjugation, as kings do with one another. This is supported by His words in another verse: ﴿and some of them would have overcome others﴾.

Our shaykh, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The correct meaning is that they would seek a way to Him through drawing near to Him and obeying Him, so how can you worship them besides Him? For if they were gods, as they claim, they would be servants of Him. He said: Several points support this:

Among them is the words of the Exalted: ﴿Those whom they call upon themselves seek the means of access (wasilah) to their Lord, [competing as to] which of them would be nearest, and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment﴾ [al-Isra' 17:57].

That is: those whom you worship besides Me are My servants, just as you are My servants, and they hope for My mercy and fear My punishment. So why do you worship them besides Me?

The second point: He, glory be to Him, did not say "they would seek a way against Him" (ʿalayhi), but said: "they would seek a way to Him" (ilayhi). This wording is used for drawing near, as in His words: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and seek the means of access (wasilah) to Him﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:35].

As for overpowering, it is used with ʿalā, as in His words: ﴿If they obey you, then do not seek a way against them﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:34].

The third point: they did not claim that their gods would overpower Him or seek to rise above Him, whereas He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Say: If there were other gods with Him, as they say...﴾. What they were saying was that their gods seek to draw near to Him and bring them closer to Him in nearness. So they were told: If the matter were as you say, those gods would be His servants; so why do you worship His servants besides Him?

Section: On the singular and plural forms of "heaven" (al-sama')

Observe how it comes in the plural in His words: ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whatever is in them glorify Him﴾ in every instance, since the intent is to report the glorification of their inhabitants, who are many and differ in their ranks, so their place had to be expressed in the plural. A parallel to this is the plural in His words: ﴿To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth, and those who are near Him are not too proud to worship Him, nor do they tire﴾.

Likewise it came in the plural in His words: ﴿The seven heavens glorify Him﴾, to report that they glorify Him through their very selves and essences despite their differing number. He emphasized this meaning by describing them with a number, and he did not limit it to "the heavens" alone but said: ﴿the seven﴾.

Observe how it came in the singular in His words: ﴿And in the heaven is your provision and what you are promised﴾. The provision is the rain, and what we are promised is Paradise, and both are in this direction, not that each one is in each of the heavens. So the singular was more fitting for it. Then consider how it came in the plural in His words: ﴿Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah﴾. Since the intent is to deny knowledge of the unseen from everyone who is in any of the heavens, He used the plural. And observe how it came in the singular, in the context of reporting the descent of water from it, only in the singular wherever it occurs, since the intent is not that it descends from the very essence of the heaven itself, but the intent is the description. This is a door Allah has opened, and you have its full course. Look into the secrets and wonders of the Book and the placement of its words, in the singular and plural, in front and behind, and its other secrets. So to Allah belongs all praise and grace; no one of His creatures can count His praise.

(Section)

As for the veil, it is found in His saying, exalted is He, quoting them: ﴿And between us and you there is a veil﴾, and His saying: ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden veil﴾.

According to the more sound of the two opinions, the meaning is: We place between the Qur'an, when you recite it, and them a veil that prevents them from understanding and reflecting upon it and from believing in it. This is clarified by His saying: ﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness﴾.

These three are the three mentioned in His saying: ﴿And they say, "Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you invite us, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a veil."﴾ So He, glorified is He, informed that He is the one who made that.

Love prevents one from seeing the truth, the coverings prevent one from understanding it, and deafness prevents one from hearing it.

Al-Kalbi said: The veil here is a barrier that prevents them from reaching the Messenger of Allah by harm, from terror and the like, which deters them from proceeding against him.

As for describing it as "hidden" (mastur), it has been said: it means "concealing" (satir), in the active sense. It has also been said: it is a relative adjective (ʿala al-nisba), meaning "in a state of concealment." The sound view is that it is on its proper pattern, i.e., hidden from the eyes so that it is not seen. The use of a passive form (maf'ul) in the sense of an active form (fa'il) is not established. The relative form in maf'ul which is not derived from its verb is like makan mahwal, i.e., possessing a hawl (turning), and rajul martub, i.e., possessing moisture. As for maf'ul which is derived from its verb, it is that upon which the action has fallen, like madrub (beaten), majruh (wounded), and mastur (concealed).

(Benefit)

Among what enters under jealousy (ghayrah) is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden veil﴾.

Al-Sarri said to his companions: Do you know what this veil is?

It is the veil of jealousy (ghayrah). And none is more jealous than Allah. Indeed, Allah, exalted is He, has not made the disbelievers worthy of understanding His speech, nor worthy of knowing Him, affirming His oneness, and loving Him. So He placed between them and His Messenger, His speech, and His tawhid a veil hidden from the eyes, out of jealousy over it, lest it be attained by one who is not worthy of it.

He said in another place in Madarij al-Salikin:

Whoever knows Him and tastes the sweetness of His nearness and love, then turns back from Him to dwelling with others, He weakens his limbs from obeying Him, shackles his heart from His will and love, delays him from the place of His nearness, and leaves him to what he has chosen for himself.

Some of them said: Beware of Him, for He is jealous; He does not like to see anything in the heart of His servant other than Himself.

From His jealousy: when His chosen one Adam inclined his heart toward Paradise and was eager for eternity therein, He expelled him from it. And from His jealousy, glorified is He: when Ibrahim, His friend, found that Isma'il had taken a portion of his heart, He commanded him to slaughter him, until he would remove from his heart that competitor.

Shirk was only a sin that is not forgiven in His sight because the heart of the polytheist is attached to Him and to other than Him. So how about one whose entire heart is attached to other than Him and who has turned away from Him completely?

If you wish to know what affliction of separation and humiliation of the veil has befallen you, look at who has enslaved your heart, who has employed your limbs, and with whom your inner self is preoccupied. Where does your heart spend the night when you lie down on your bed? And where does it fly when you awake from your sleep? That is your worshipped one and your god. So when you hear the call on the Day of Resurrection: "Let every people follow what they used to worship," you will go with him, whoever he may be.

There is no god but Allah! How severe is the loss of one who sells the finest life in this abode, which is connected to the good life there, and everlasting bliss, for a life of turmoil and wretchedness connected to painful punishment; and the duration is an hour of a day, or an evening or its forenoon, or a day or part of a day, in which is the gain of eternity or the loss of eternity.

﻿So it is nothing but an hour, then it passes, and all of this goes away and vanishes.

(Another Benefit)

Here is a subtle kind of the Lord's jealousy, exalted and glorified is He, which minds do not reach: that a servant is granted a door of purity, intimacy, and existence, so he dwells in it, is at ease with it, and his soul delights in it, and he becomes preoccupied with it from the intended goal. Then his true Master becomes jealous over him, empties him of it, and returns him then to Himself through poverty, humility, and neediness, making him witness the utmost of his poverty and annihilation, and that he has nothing of his own self whatsoever. Thus the honor of that intimacy, purity, and existence turns into abasement, neediness, poverty, and dependence. A single atom of this is more beloved to Him, glorified and exalted is He, and more beneficial to the servant, than towering mountains of that purity and intimacy stripped of witnessing poverty, humility, and neediness. This is a door that no heart can contain.

(Section) Among jealousy is the jealousy over subtle knowledge, and over what the listener's understanding cannot grasp, that it be mentioned to him. It is for this jealousy that ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Speak to people in terms of what they know. Do you want Allah and His Messenger to be denied?"

And Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "You will not speak to a people with a statement that their minds cannot reach except that it will be a trial for some of them."

So the scholar is jealous of his knowledge, that he should not spend it on those who are not its people or place it in other than its proper place, as ʿIsa ibn Maryam said: "O Children of Israel, do not withhold wisdom from its people, lest you wrong them; and do not give it to those who are not its people, lest you wrong it."

Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, was asked about the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: "Allah is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them."

He said to the questioner: "What assures you that if I inform you of its interpretation you will not disbelieve? For you would deny it, and your denial of it is your disbelief in it."

So the subtle, delicate issue that is given to those who are not its people is like a beautiful woman who is delivered to a blind, paralyzed man, as it is said:

A bride conducted to a blind, paralyzed man.

And Abu ʿAli, whenever something disturbed the course of his gathering from the disorder of the moment, would say: "This is from the jealousy of the Truth," meaning that what happens of disruption of the clarity of the moment should not occur.

(Section)

As for His saying, may He be exalted, concerning the disbelievers, that they said: ﴿You follow none but a man bewitched﴾, and the saying of the people of Salih to him: ﴿You are only one of the bewitched﴾, it has been said that what is meant is one who has a sahr, which is the lung (ri'ah), meaning that he is a human being like them who eats and drinks, not an angel. According to this view, the word does not mean "sorcery." But this answer is unsatisfactory and is extremely far-fetched, for the disbelievers did not describe a human being as "bewitched," and this usage is not known in any language. Whenever they wished to express this meaning, they used the explicit word "human being," saying: ﴿You are only human beings like us﴾, ﴿Shall we believe two humans like ourselves?﴾, ﴿Has God sent a human as a messenger?﴾

As for "bewitched" (maskhur), they did not mean by it one who has a sahr, which is the lung. What relevance would the mention of the lung have in this context? Moreover, how could Pharaoh say to Moses: ﴿Indeed, I think you, O Moses, are bewitched﴾, could he have not known that he was a human being? And how would Moses answer him with: ﴿And indeed, I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed﴾? If he had meant by "bewitched" that he was a human being, Moses would have confirmed it and said: "Yes, I am a human being whom God has sent to you," just as the messengers said to their peoples when those peoples said to them: ﴿You are only human beings like us﴾, and they replied: ﴿We are only human beings like you﴾, and did not deny it. So this answer is extremely weak.

A group, including Ibn Jarir and others, answered that "bewitched" here means one who has been taught magic by another, so that "maskhur" in their view means "sahir," i.e., one who knows magic. This is good if the language supports it, namely that one who has learned magic is called maskhur. But this is hardly recognized in usage or in the language. Rather, "maskhur" is one who has been bewitched by someone else, like "matbub" (one who has been afflicted), "madrub" (one who has been struck), and "maqtul" (one who has been killed) and similar forms. As for one who has learned magic, he is called "sahir," meaning one who knows magic, even if no one has bewitched him, as the people of Pharaoh said to Moses: ﴿Indeed, this is a knowledgeable sorcerer﴾. Pharaoh charged him with being bewitched, and his people charged him with being a sorcerer. So the correct view is the third answer, which is the answer of the author of al-Kashshaf and others: that "maskhur" is used in its proper sense, from "suhira" until he became deranged, so they said "maskhur," like "majnun" (one whose reason has departed), who does not understand what he says. For one who is "bewitched" in this sense is one whose mind has become so corrupt that he does not know what he is saying, and so he is like a madman. This is why they said of him, "a bewitched madman" (mu'allim majnun). As for one who is afflicted in his body with one of the illnesses that afflict people, this does not prevent others from following him. The enemies of the messengers did not accuse them of bodily illnesses; they accused them of what would warn their foolish followers away from them, namely that they had been bewitched until they no longer knew what they were saying, like madmen. This is why God, the Exalted, said: ﴿See how they strike similitudes for you, so they have gone astray and cannot find a way﴾.

They described you as a poet once, as a sorcerer another time, as a madman once, and as bewitched another time. They went astray in all of this like one who seeks a path in his bewilderment and confusion, but whichever way he takes is a path of error and confusion, so he is perplexed in his affair, unable to find the right way or to walk it. Such is the condition of the enemies of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) with him, until they struck for him similitudes from which God had cleared him, though he was the furthest of God's creation from them, and every intelligent person knows that they are lies, fabrication and calumny.

As for your claim that the bewitchment of prophets contradicts God's protection of them: He, glorified is He, protects them, guards them, preserves them and takes charge of them, yet He tests them with whatever He wills of harm from the disbelievers, so that they may merit the perfection of His honor, so that those who come after them from their nations and successors may find solace in them when they are harmed by people, seeing what befell the messengers and prophets, and so they endure, are content, and take them as a model. Also, so that the cup of the disbelievers may be filled, and they deserve what has been prepared for them of immediate punishment and deferred retribution; He will then destroy them for their transgression and enmity, and hasten the cleansing of the earth of them. This is part of His wisdom, exalted is He, in testing His prophets and messengers with the harm of their people. His is the consummate wisdom and the abundant blessing; there is no god but Him, and no lord besides Him.

(Section)

Reflect on how these words, despite their brevity, conciseness and eloquence, comprise the principle (aṣl), the derivative (far'), the cause (ʿillah) and the ruling (ḥukm).

He, glorified is He, responded to them with a rebuttal that contains a decisive proof of His power to restore them as a new creation. He said: ﴿Say: Be you stones or iron, or a creation of what is greater in your breasts.﴾ ﴿They will say: "Who will restore us?" Say: "He who originated you the first time."﴾

When they considered it improbable that Allah would restore them as a new creation after they had become bones and crumbled dust, it was said to them: "Be stones or iron, or a creation of what is greater in your breasts," whether it be death, or the sky, or the earth, or any creation you deem great and which looms large in your breasts. The essence of the proof is that you are nurtured, created and subjugated to what your Creator wills, and you cannot alter your states from one form to another form that does not accept dissolution, such as stones and iron. Moreover, even if you were in this form of strength and hardness, My decrees, My power and My will would still take effect, and you would neither precede Me nor escape Me. This is like one who says to someone within his grip: "Ascend to the sky, for I will overtake you"; meaning, if you ascended to the sky, I would overtake you. Accordingly, the meaning of the verse is: even if you were stones or iron, or a creation greater than that, you would not defeat Me, nor would you escape Me.

It was also said: the meaning is, "Be stones or iron in your own estimation": imagine yourselves and consider yourselves a creation that does not perish or disintegrate, for We will cause you to die, then We will revive you and restore you as a new creation. There is a subtle difference between the two meanings. The first meaning implies that even if you were able to transfer your form from one state to another that is harder and stronger, Our will and power would still take effect upon you, and you would not be able to thwart Us; so how much more so when you are incapable of that? The second meaning implies that you should imagine yourselves and place yourselves in this position, then consider whether you could escape Us and defeat Us, or whether Our power and will encompass you even if you were thus. This is among the most eloquent of decisive proofs, in which no doubt whatsoever can arise; rather, sound minds cannot help but submit to and yield to it. When the people recognized the soundness of this proof and that it was self-evident, they shifted to demanding who would restore them, saying: "Who will restore us?" Whether this was a question seeking to identify the restorer or a denial of it, it is among the most ugly and clear forms of obstinacy. For this reason, its answer was: ﴿Say: He who originated you the first time.﴾

When the people knew that this was a decisive answer, they moved to another avenue of obstinacy, namely asking about the time of this restoration, so they shook their heads toward it and said: "When will it be?" Then the Exalted said: ﴿Say: It may be that it is near.﴾

So let the discerning consider the subtle placement of this proof, and its necessary implication of what it signifies, an implication from which there is no escape, and how it contains the questions and the answers to them in the most eloquent, correct and clear manner. How much is lost to those who turn away from reflecting on the Qur'an and substitute for it the refuse of minds and the chaff of thoughts!

(Another section)

Reflect on the answers given to each question in detail. They first said: "When we are bones and crumbled dust, shall we indeed be raised as a new creation?" In answer to this question it was said to them: If you claim that you have no Creator and no Lord, then why not be a new creation that death does not destroy, like stones and iron, or something even greater in your breasts? If you say, "We have a Lord and Creator who created us in this form and brought us into this existence which does not accept permanence, and did not make us stones or iron," then the proof has been established against you by your own acknowledgment. What, then, stands between your Creator and Originator and restoring you as a new creation?

There is another formulation of the argument: if you were of stone, iron, or a creation greater than them, He would still be capable of annihilating you, transforming your essences, and moving them from one state to another.

And whoever is capable of acting upon these bodies with their hardness and firmness, by annihilating them, transforming them and moving them from one state to another, then what would prevent Him from acting upon what is lesser than them, by annihilating it, transforming it and moving it from one state to another?

He, glorified is He, then informed that they would ask another question by saying "Who will restore us?" when our bodies have transformed and perished. He answered them with His saying: ﴿Say: He who originated you the first time.﴾

This answer is similar to the answer to the questioner's saying: ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ [Yā-Sīn: 78]. When the argument seized them, its ruling bound them, and they found no escape from it, they moved to another question by which they excused themselves, as one defeated in argument excuses himself with such things, namely their saying "When is it?" They were answered with His saying:

﴿It may be that it is near, the Day He calls you, and you will respond with His praise, and you will think that you remained only a little.﴾

(Fa'idah)
Fear is one of the three pillars of faith and excellence (ihsan) upon which the stations of all the wayfarers (al-salikin) revolve: fear (al-khawf), hope (al-raja'), and love (al-mahabbah). Allah, glorified is He, mentioned them in His saying: ﴿Say: Call upon those whom you claim besides Him; they possess not the removal of harm from you, nor its transfer. Those whom they call upon seek means of access to their Lord, [striving to be] nearest to Him, and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment﴾ [al-Isra' 17:56-57].
So He combined the three stations, for seeking the means (ibtigha' al-wasilah) to Him is drawing near to Him through His love and doing what He loves. Then He says: ﴿and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment﴾, mentioning love, fear and hope. The meaning is that those you call upon besides Allah, from among the angels, prophets and righteous ones, draw near to their Lord, fear Him and hope in Him. They are His servants just as you are His servants, so why do you worship them besides Him when you and they are both servants of His?
(Fasl)
Among the stations of "Thee alone do we worship, and Thee alone do we ask for help" is the station of hope (al-raja').
Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Those whom they call upon seek means of access to their Lord, [striving to be] nearest to Him, and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment﴾ [al-Isra' 17:57]. The seeking of the means to Him is the pursuit of nearness to Him through servitude ('ubudiyyah) and love. Thus He mentioned the three stations of faith upon which it is built: love, fear and hope. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah, then the term of Allah is surely coming﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:5]. He also said: ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾ [al-Kahf 18:110]. And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Those hope for the mercy of Allah, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:218].
In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say, three days before his death: "None of you should die except while thinking well of his Lord." And in the Sahih, from him (ﷺ): "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: I am as My servant thinks of Me, so let him think of Me what he wills."
"Hope" (al-raja') is a driver that drives the hearts toward the lands of the Beloved, and He is Allah and the Last Abode, and the journey becomes pleasant for them.
It was said: it is the joyful expectation of the generosity and grace of the Lord, blessed and exalted, and the delight in contemplating His bounty, glorified is He.
It was said: it is confidence in the generosity of the Lord, exalted is He.
The difference between it and wishful thinking (al-tamanni) is that wishful thinking occurs with laziness, and does not lead its possessor on the path of earnestness and striving, whereas "hope" occurs with exerting effort and good reliance (tawakkul).
The first is like the state of one who wishes to have land which he would sow and harvest its crop.
The second is like the state of one who plows his land, tills it and sows it, and hopes for the sprouting of the crop.
For this reason the scholars ('arifun) unanimously agreed that hope is not valid except with action.
Shah al-Karmani said: the sign of the soundness of hope is the goodness of obedience.
Hope is of three kinds: two are praiseworthy, and one is a blameworthy delusion.
The first two are the hope of a man who acts in obedience to Allah upon a light from Allah; so he hopes for its reward. And a man who committed sins and then repented of them; so he hopes for the forgiveness of Allah, the Exalted, His pardon, His kindness, His generosity, His forbearance and His nobility.
The third: a man persisting in negligence and sins, who hopes for the mercy of Allah without action. This is the delusion, the wishful thinking and the false hope.
The wayfarer has two perspectives: a perspective on himself, his faults and the blights of his deeds, which opens for him the door of fear, and a perspective on the vastness of the grace, generosity and kindness of his Lord, which opens for him the door of hope.
For this reason it was said in defining hope: it is looking at the vastness of the mercy of Allah.
Abu 'Ali al-Rudhbari said: fear and hope are like the two wings of a bird: when they are balanced the bird stands upright and its flight is complete; if one of them diminishes, deficiency enters it; and if both depart, the bird is in the state of death.
Ahmad ibn 'Asim was asked: What is the sign of hope in the servant? He said: that when favour surrounds him he is inspired with gratitude, hoping for the completion of the blessing from Allah upon him in this world and the Hereafter, and the completion of His pardon for him in the Hereafter.
They differed as to which of the two hopes is more perfect: the hope of the doer of good for the reward of his good deeds, or the hope of the sinner who repents for the forgiveness and pardon of his Lord?
One group preferred the hope of the doer of good, because the causes of hope are stronger with him. Another group preferred the hope of the sinner, because his hope is free from the defect of seeing one's own deed, and is joined with the humility of seeing one's sin.
Yahya ibn Mu'adh said: My hope in You along with sins nearly overcomes my hope in You along with deeds; for I find myself relying in deeds upon sincerity, and how shall I purify and secure them, when I am known for blights? And I find myself in sins relying upon Your pardon, and how would You not forgive them when You are described as bountiful?
He also said: My God, the sweetest of gifts in my heart is Your hope; the sweetest of speech on my tongue is Your praise; and the dearest of hours to me is the hour in which Your meeting occurs.
(Fasl)
Hope is among the most noble, highest and most honourable of their stations. Upon it, and upon love and fear, revolves the journey to Allah. Allah, the Exalted, has praised its people and commended them, saying: ﴿Indeed there has been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent pattern for whoever hopes for Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah often﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:21].
In the authentic divine hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ), what he narrates from his Lord, Mighty and Majestic: "O son of Adam, as long as you call upon Me and hope in Me, I will forgive you for what you have done, and I do not mind." Al-A'mash narrated from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him. When he remembers Me in himself, I remember him in Myself; and if he remembers Me in an assembly, I remember him in an assembly better than theirs; if he draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit; if he draws near to Me a cubit, I draw near to him a fathom; and if he comes to Me walking, I come to him running." Narrated by Muslim.
Allah, the Exalted, has informed us about the special servants of His, whom the polytheists used to claim they drew near to Allah through: that they were hoping in Him and fearing Him. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: Call upon those whom you claim besides Him; they possess not the removal of harm from you, nor its transfer. Those whom they call upon seek means of access to their Lord, [striving to be] nearest to Him, and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is ever feared﴾ [al-Isra' 17:56].
Allah, the Exalted, says: These whom you call upon besides Me are My servants; they draw near to Me through My obedience, hope for My mercy, and fear My punishment; so why do you call upon them besides Me? He thus praised them by the best of their states and stations: love, fear and hope.
His saying: "because it is an opposition from one aspect and an objection from another aspect."
It is said: and it is servitude and attachment to Allah from the standpoint of His name, the Benevolent, the Kind; that attachment and worship through this name and knowledge of Allah is what necessitates hope in the servant, whether he is aware of it or not. So the strength of hope is according to the strength of knowledge of Allah, His names and attributes, and the dominance of His mercy over His wrath. Were it not for the spirit of hope, the servitude of the heart and limbs would be suspended, and the monasteries, churches, prayers and mosques in which the name of Allah is much mentioned would be demolished. Indeed, were it not for the spirit of hope, the limbs would not move in obedience; and were it not for its good fragrance, the ships of deeds would not sail on the sea of intentions. And I have verses:
- Were it not for attachment to hope, the soul of the lover would be cut off in grief and torn apart,
- And likewise, were it not for its coolness amid the heat of livers that melted in veiling and burned,
- Could there ever be a lover of love who is not seen attached to his beloved by his hope?
- Or, as love for Him grows strong, does hope grow strong too, increasing in longing?
- Were it not for hope driving the mounts, they would not travel with their loads, hoping for meeting, toward their dwelling.
According to the measure of love and its strength is hope. Every lover is necessarily hoping and fearing; he is most hopeful of his beloved when he is most beloved to him. Likewise is his fear: he fears falling from his beloved's eyes, his beloved's rejection of him, his distance, and his being veiled from Him; so his fear is the most intense fear. And his hope is intrinsic to love, for he hopes for Him before meeting Him and attaining Him. When he meets Him and attains Him, his hope intensifies, because of the life of his spirit that comes to him through it, the delight of his heart through the kindnesses of his beloved, His goodness and His turning towards him, His looking upon him with the eye of contentment, His qualifying him for His love, and other things that the lover has no life, delight or success except by reaching Him from his beloved. So his hope is the greatest hope, and the most sublime and complete.
So ponder this point with true contemplation, and it will reveal to you great secrets of the secrets of servitude and love. Every love is accompanied by fear and hope, and in proportion to its firmness in the heart of the lover, his fear and hope intensify; but the fear of the lover is not accompanied by desolation, unlike the fear of the evildoer; and the hope of the lover is not accompanied by a defect, unlike the hope of the hired worker. How far is the hope of the lover from the hope of the hired worker? Between them is as much as between their two states.
In sum: hope is essential for the aspirant wayfarer, and if the knower were parted from it for a moment he would perish or nearly so. For he revolves between a sin for which he hopes for forgiveness, a fault for which he hopes for correction, a righteous deed for which he hopes for acceptance, uprightness for which he hopes for its attainment and continuance, and nearness to Allah and a station with Him to which he hopes to arrive. None of the wayfarers is free of these matters, or some of them.
(Fasl)
There is no opposition, in hope or in supplication, to the disposal of the Owner in His dominion. For he hopes that He will dispose of His dominion also in the way that is most fitting and most beloved of the two matters to Him: grace is more beloved to Him than justice, pardon more beloved to Him than retribution, leniency more beloved to Him than exact requital, leaving more beloved to Him than exacting; and His mercy overcame His wrath.
So the one who hopes has attached his hope to His beloved and pleasing disposal. His hope has not entailed his going out of His disposal in His dominion; rather it required his servitude and the attainment of the most beloved of the two dispositions to Him. He, glorified and exalted, does not benefit from exacting His right and punishing His servant, such that his hope would nullify that. Rather, the servant himself sought punishment and took his right from himself through his polytheism and disbelief in Allah, and his striving toward His wrath. And for His wrath there are consequences, effects and requirements, and the servant prefers them, strives to attain them, and acts upon them by preferring them and striving for their causes. So he is the one who destroys himself. And his Lord warns him, makes him see, and calls out to him: "Come to Me, I will give you shelter and protection, deliver you from what you fear, and secure you from all that you dread." But he refuses except to flee from Him and shy away from Him, to make peace with His enemy, to support him against his Lord, and to seek the pleasure of the creature through the things that displease the Creator. The pleasure of the creature is more preferred by him than the pleasure of his Creator; the right of the creature is more binding upon him than the right of the Creator; and his fear, hope and love in his heart are greater than his fear of Allah, his hope in Him and his love for Him. So he has not left any way to the bounty, honour and reward of his Lord toward him; rather he has blocked the channels leading to them with all his effort, and has handed himself over to His enemy, made peace with him, listened to him and obeyed him, and submitted to his pleasures. Thus he has committed injustice of the worst and most severe kind.
So he is the one who opposed what He wanted from him with his own desire, his whim and his appetite; he stood in the way of what He loves and what pleases Him, repelling it, and did not permit it to enter upon him. He wasted his share, diminished his right, wronged himself, opposed his beloved, befriended his enemy, displeased Him with his life in seeking His pleasure, and pleased Him with his life in seeking His displeasure. He gave his soul generously to his enemy, and withheld it stingily from his beloved and his protector.

The Lord, blessed and exalted, has no grievance against His servant that He would overtake him with His punishment, nor does He find satisfaction in his chastisement, nor does that add to His dominion the weight of an atom of His dominion. How could it be otherwise, when His mercy is broader than His punishment, precedes His wrath, and prevails over it? He has prescribed mercy for Himself. Thus the servant's hope in Him does not diminish anything of His wisdom, nor reduce an atom of His sovereignty, nor take Him out of the perfection of His disposal, nor necessitate what contradicts His perfection, nor the suspension of His attributes and names. Had it not been that the servant himself is the one who blocked for himself the paths of good and shut the doors of mercy against himself by his own poor choice for his soul, his Lord would have been to him above his hope and above his expectation.

As for the servant's submission to his Lord, his surrender by casting himself down before Him, and his contentment with the places of His judgment concerning him, this is nothing but hope on his part that He will have mercy on him, forgive his slip, pardon him, accept his good deeds despite the defects and blights of his actions, and overlook his bad deeds. So the strength of his hope necessitated this submission, compliance, and casting himself at the door. This cannot be conceived without hope at all. Hope is the life of seeking, and desire is its spirit.

And He, glory be to Him, described Thamud as having disbelieved with knowledge and insight into the truth. For this reason He said: ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a clear sign, but they wronged her with it﴾.

That is, a clear, illuminating proof. This is like His saying: ﴿And We made the sign of the day visible﴾, meaning illuminating. The literal meaning of the word is that it makes whoever sees it a seer, so it gives him sight and makes him see, that is, it makes him one who has sight. So it is evident and clarifying. It is said "basura bihi" when one sees it, like His saying: ﴿So she watched him from afar﴾, and His saying: ﴿I perceived what they did not perceive﴾.

As for "abṣarahu" (he made him see), it has two meanings. The first is to make him one who sees a thing, that is, one who has sight of it, as in the sign of the day and the sign of Thamud. The second is to mean "ra'ahu" (he saw it), as when you say "I saw Zayd."

In the hadith of Abu Shurayh al-Adawi: "I will relate to you a saying that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of the Conquest. My ears heard it, my heart retained it, and my eyes saw him when he spoke it."

From this is His saying: ﴿So turn away from them for a time, and watch them, for they will see﴾.

It has been said that the meaning is: "watch them" concerning what will be decreed against them of captivity, killing and punishment in the Hereafter, "for they will see" you, and what will be decreed for you of victory, support and a good end.

The intent is to bring the one who sees near to the one addressed, until it is as if it were set before his eyes and he saw those who look at him.

The point is that the sign gave them insight, yet they preferred misguidance and disbelief with knowledge and certainty. For this reason, and Allah knows best, He mentioned their story among the stories of the other nations in the surah "By the sun and its brightness" (al-Shams, surah 91), because in it He mentioned the division of souls into the purified, rightly guided and well-directed, and the corrupt, astray and misguided. In it He also mentioned the two foundations, the divine decree (qadar) and the revealed law (shar'), so He said: ﴿And He inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness﴾. This is His decree and His ordainment.

Then He said: ﴿He has succeeded who purifies it, and he has failed who corrupts it﴾. This is His command and His religion. As for Thamud, they were guided, but they preferred blindness over guidance. So He mentioned their story to show the evil end of one who prefers wickedness over piety, and corrupting the soul over purifying it. Allah knows best what He intended.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: "It was a vision of the eye, which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was shown on the night of his Night Journey (al-Isrāʾ). Despite this, in the morning he was among them and his state had not changed; no swooning or fainting came upon him, and he told them the details of what he had seen, not being annihilated from himself or from his witnessing. For this reason his state was more perfect than the state of Mūsā ibn ʿImrān, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon them both, when he fell down in a swoon when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain and made it crumble to dust."

Beneath this objection lies a meaning: "Tell me, why did You honor him over me?" The depth of this objection is that what You did is neither wise nor right, and that wisdom required that he prostrate to me, because the inferior submits to the superior. So why did You oppose wisdom?

Then he followed that with preferring himself over him and belittling him, saying: ﴿I am better than him﴾ [al-A'raf: 12].

Then he confirmed this with his refuted argument, preferring his substance and origin over the substance and origin of Adam, peace be upon him. These premises yielded for him his refusal and his abstention from prostration, and his disobedience to the Lord who is worshipped. So he combined ignorance and injustice, arrogance, envy and disobedience, and the opposing of a text with opinion and reason. He humiliated himself with every humiliation from the very direction in which he sought to exalt himself, placed himself low from the very direction in which he sought elevation, abased himself from the very direction in which he sought honor, and inflicted upon himself every pain from the very direction in which he sought pleasure. He did to himself what, even if the greatest of his enemies strove to harm him, he could not have reached such a degree. And one whose deceit toward himself is this, how can a sensible person listen to him, accept him, and take him as an ally?

(A Benefit)

Regarding the words of the Exalted to Iblis: ﴿Go, and whoever follows you among them—indeed, Hell is your recompense, a full recompense.﴾

He returned the pronoun in the form of address, although "whoever follows you" would call for the third person. This is because a addressee and an absent party were combined, so the addressee was given precedence, and the absent party was made subordinate to him, just as they were subordinate to him in disobedience and in punishment. Thus it was fitting to make them subordinate to him in the wording.

This is among the fine instances of the wording's connection with the meaning and its linkage to it. The word "jaza'an mawfuran" (a full recompense) is in the accusative, according to Ibn Malik, as an absolute object (maṣdar), and its governing element, in his view, is the first verbal noun. He said: a verbal noun can govern a verbal noun; you say, "I was amazed at your standing (qiyamaka) standing (qiyaman)." The verb may also govern it, as in "qiyam qiyaman," and the active participle (ism al-fa'il), as in his saying:

"So I have become one who does not approach the seductress,
restrained from her desire with a restraint."

And the passive participle (ism al-maf'ul) is "maṭlūb ṭalaban" (sought with a seeking).

Beyond this, there are two other opinions regarding the accusative of "jaza'":

First: it is governed by what is implied in "fa-inna Jahannama jaza'ukum" (indeed, Hell is your recompense), from the verb, since it implies "tujazawna" (you will be recompensed), and that is the governing element of "jaza'."

Second: it is a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl), and the occurrence of a verbal noun as a ḥāl is permissible here because it is qualified (by "mawfuran").

Al-Zamakhshari mentioned these two opinions, and this is like your saying, "Take your portion, a full portion."

What appears from the verse is that "jaza'" is not a verbal noun; rather, it is a name for share and portion. So it is not the verbal noun of "jazaytuhu jaza'" (I recompensed him a recompense); rather, it is like "'aṭā'" (gift) and "naṣīb" (portion). This is why He described it as "mawfuran," meaning complete, without deficiency. On this basis, its accusative is by specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), which resembles the accusative of detached qualifiers (ṣifāt maqṭū'a). This is as al-Zamakhshari and others said regarding the words of the Exalted: ﴿For men is a share of what the parents and the close relatives leave, and for women is a share﴾ up to His words: ﴿a share ordained﴾. He said: its accusative is by specification, meaning "I mean a share ordained." It is also permissible that it be in the accusative of emphatic verbal nouns, like His words: ﴿an obligation from Allah﴾.

Consider His Exalted words: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those you call upon vanish, except Him﴾. Note how He used (idhā, "when") here, since the touching of harm to them at sea was certain, unlike His words: ﴿Man does not tire of asking for good, but if evil touches him, he becomes despairing and hopeless﴾.

For there He did not restrict the touching of evil, but left it unrestricted. When He restricted it to the sea, where it is certain to occur, He used the particle (idhā).

Death is certain.

I say: the conditional is not attached to death in general, but to a particular kind of death, namely death without a child.

If you say: What then do you make of His words: ﴿O you who believe, eat of the good things We have provided you, and give thanks to God, if you truly worship Him﴾,

and His words: ﴿So eat of that over which the name of God has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs﴾? The Arabs also say: "If you are my son, obey me." Therefore glory be to Him who clothed him with all the garments of honour: reason, knowledge, eloquence, speech, a comely form, a fine appearance, an upright stature, the acquisition of sciences through inference and reflection, and the acquiring of noble and virtuous character traits of piety, obedience and submission. The angels who bear the Throne of the Most Merciful and those around it seek forgiveness for him; the angels assigned to him guard him; those assigned to rain and plants strive for his provision and work on it; the spheres have been subjected, moving in compliance, revolving with what serves his interests; the sun, the moon and the stars are subjected and running by the reckoning of his times and seasons and the regulation of his sustenance. Those who held this view answered the question of the disbelievers' seeing on the Day of Resurrection by saying that Allah will bring them out of their graves to the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection seeing, and they will be gathered from the place of standing to the Fire blind.

This was said by al-Farra' and others.

(Section)

The return (al-ma'ad) for the servant on that Day consists of what was present for him in this world. For this reason the Day of Recompense is so named. Allah said: ﴿And whoever is blind in this [world] will be blind in the Hereafter and further astray from the way﴾, and ﴿And Allah increases in guidance those who are guided...﴾ [Maryam: 76], to the end of the verse.

Whoever felt estrangement from Allah in this abode through his disobedience to Him, his estrangement from Him in the barzakh (the intermediate realm between death and resurrection) and on the Day of Return will be greater and more severe. Whoever found his eye comforted by Him in "this life," the world, will have his eye comforted by Him on the Day of Resurrection, at death, and on the Day of Resurrection. The servant dies in the state in which he lived, and is resurrected in the state in which he died, and his deeds return to him exactly, so he is blessed by them outwardly and inwardly. They bring him joy, happiness, pleasure, delight, comfort of the eye, bliss, strength of heart, good tidings, life, expansion of the breast, and contentment, which are among the finest, greatest, purest, and most delightful blessings. Is blessing anything other than the goodness of the soul, the joy and happiness of the heart, its gladness, its expansion, and its good tidings? Besides this, there arises for him from his deeds whatever his soul desires and his eye finds delightful among the various desirable things that souls crave and eyes enjoy. The variety of those desirable things, their perfection, and their reaching the level of beauty and suitability depend on the perfection of his deed, his following of the Prophet's way in it, his sincerity, and his reaching the level of excellence (ihsan) in it, and according to its variety. Whoever's deeds that please Allah and are beloved to Him in this abode were varied, the kinds in which he takes pleasure in that abode will be varied and increased for him according to the increase of his deeds here. His increase in those varieties, his delight in them, and his enjoyment of obtaining them there will be in proportion to his increase in deeds and their variety here. Allah, glory be to Him, has made for every one of the deeds, both those beloved to Him and those He abhors, an effect, a recompense, a pleasure, and a pain specific to it, such that the effect and recompense of one does not resemble those of another.

For this reason the pleasures of the people of Paradise and the pains of the people of the Fire are varied, and the good things and punishments in them are varied. The pleasure of one who strikes in every avenue of Allah's pleasure with an arrow and takes a share from each is not like the pleasure of one who develops his arrow and share in a single kind of them. Nor is the pain of one who strikes in every avenue of Allah's displeasure with a share like the pain of one who strikes with a single arrow into His displeasures.

The Prophet (ﷺ) indicated that the perfection of the good things one enjoys in the Hereafter is in proportion to the perfection of the deeds he did in this world corresponding to them (... "He saw a cluster of bad dates (hashf) hanging in the mosque for charity, and said: 'The owner of this will eat bad dates on the Day of Resurrection.'")

So he informed that his recompense will be of the same kind as his deed, and he will be rewarded for that charity with bad dates of the same kind.

**[Section: The strength of faith and knowledge, by which its possessor is pardoned in matters for which others are not pardoned]**

Those who held this view argued with what is in the Sahih from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The virtue of the congregational prayer over the prayer of one person is twenty-five degrees."

Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Sahih.

The proponents of the first view said: This does not contradict our statement, which is that Allah, glorified is He, and the angels of the night and the day witness the recitation of dawn. The intended meaning is not general witnessing, for Allah is a witness over everything, but a particular witnessing, namely the witnessing of presence and closeness, linked to the nearness of the Lord, exalted is He, and His descent to the lowest heaven in the last third of the night.

Al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated: Ziyadah ibn Muhammad told me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Fadalah ibn Ubayd al-Ansari, from Abu al-Darda, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said:

"Allah, Mighty and Majestic, descends during three hours that remain of the night. In the first hour He opens the Remembrance (*al-Dhikr*) which no one but Him sees, so Allah erases what He wills and establishes. Then in the second hour He descends to the Garden of Eden, which is His abode that no eye has seen and that has not occurred to the heart of any human; it is His dwelling, and no one of the children of Adam dwells with Him there except three: the prophets, the truthful ones and the martyrs. Then He says: 'Blessed is the one who has entered you.' Then in the third hour He descends to the lowest heaven with His spirit and His angels, and He says: 'Stand up, by My might,' and then He looks down upon His servants and says: 'Is there any seeker of forgiveness that I may forgive him? Is there any petitioner who asks Me that I may give him? Is there any supplicant who calls upon Me that I may answer him?' until the dawn prayer."

This is particular to the dawn prayer and is not shared by other prayers. This does not contradict the continuation of the descent in the other hadiths until the rising of dawn, especially since it is conditioned in some of them upon the breaking of dawn, which is the spreading of its light.

This would not occur except with great earliness at the beginning of the time, so that the recitation falls in the time of the descent, and the particular witnessing takes place. Moreover, a hadith has come explicitly stating the continuation of this until the conclusion of the dawn prayer. Who is asking Me that I may give him? Who is seeking forgiveness from Me that I may forgive him?' until the dawn rises, or the reciter finishes the dawn prayer."

Many have narrated this from Muhammad [ibn Amr], among them Sulayman ibn Bilal, Isma'il ibn Ja'far, al-Darawardi, Hafs ibn Ghiyath, Yazid ibn Harun, Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata, Muhammad ibn Ja'far, and al-Nadr ibn Shumayl; all of them said: "or the reciter finishes the dawn prayer." If this wording is preserved from the Prophet ﷺ, it is explicit in meaning and reveals the intended sense. If it is not preserved, and it was from the doubt of the narrator as to whether he said this or that, then we have already stated that there is no conflict between the two wordings.

The hadith of al-Layth ibn Sa'd from Muhammad ibn Ziyad indicates the continuation of the descent until the time of the dawn prayer, and that its linking to the rising [of dawn] is because it is the first time in which the ascent occurs. This is as narrated by Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, from his father, from al-Aghurr Abu Muslim, who said: "I bear witness upon the Prophet ﷺ that he said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, delays until, when a third of the night has passed, He descends to this heaven. Then He commands the gates of the heaven, and they are opened. Then He says: Is there anyone asking, that I may give him? Is there anyone calling, that I may answer him? Is there anyone seeking forgiveness, that I may forgive him? Is there anyone seeking relief, that I may relieve him? Is there anyone in distress, that I may remove it from him? He remains in that station until the dawn rises every night in the world, and then He ascends to the heaven.'"

Al-Daraqutni said: Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq added a good addition to it. The purpose of mentioning nearness to the Imam in the dawn prayer and the early performance of it at the beginning of its time is this. And Allah knows best.
