Al-Daraqutni said: Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq added a good addition to it. The purpose of mentioning nearness to the Imam in the dawn prayer and the early performance of it at the beginning of its time is this. And Allah knows best.

**[Section: The strength of faith and knowledge, by which its possessor is pardoned in matters for which others are not pardoned]**

If it is said: You have mentioned that the one who loves is forgiven what others are not forgiven, and that the close friend (al-waliyy) is excused what is not excused for others. Likewise the scholar, who is forgiven what the ignorant person is not forgiven, as al-Tabarani narrated with a good *isnad* (chain of narration), traced back to the Prophet ﷺ: "When Allah, glorified is He, gathers the people on the Day of Resurrection in one level plain, He will say to the scholars: 'I was worshipped by your fatwas, and I know that you used to mix [with the people] just as the people mix. I did not place My knowledge in you intending to punish you. Go, for I have forgiven you.'" This is the meaning of the hadith, and it has been transmitted both *musnad* (with a complete chain) and *mursal* (with a broken chain).

This which you have mentioned is correct, and it is what wisdom, generosity and excellence require. But what will you do with the doubled punishment that has been threatened against those [close ones] if something disliked occurs from them? Such as His saying, ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality, the punishment will be doubled for her, double﴾ [al-Ahzab: 30].

And His saying, ﴿And had We not made you firm, you would almost have inclined toward them a little. Then We would have made you taste double [punishment] in life and double in death; then you would not find for yourself any helper against Us﴾ [al-Isra: 74-75].

That is: Had We not made you firm, you would have nearly inclined toward them to some extent, and if you had done so, We would have made you taste double the punishment of life and double the punishment of death; that is, We would have doubled the punishment for you in this world and the Hereafter. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta﴾ [al-Haqqah: 44-46]. That is: if he had brought something from his own self, We would have seized him by his right hand, severed the sinew of his heart, and destroyed him. Allah protected him from inclining to his enemies even by a particle of his heart, and from fabricating against Him, glorified is He. How many have inclined to His enemies and fabricated against Him from their own selves, yet He has granted them respite and paid them no heed, such as all the people of innovations (*ahl al-bid'ah*), who fabricate against His names, His attributes and His religion.

What you have mentioned about the story of Yunus is of this same category, for he was not excused for one display of anger, and he was imprisoned on account of it in the belly of the fish. And the case of the father of mankind suffices, for he was not excused for a single morsel, and it was the cause of his expulsion from the Garden.

The answer is that this is also true, and there is no contradiction between the two matters. Whoever has been perfected in Allah's blessing, and has been singled out from it with what others have not been singled out with, in being given what others have been deprived of, is favoured with bounties, honoured with generosity, singled out for greater nearness, and placed in the station of the beloved friend. His condition requires that he preserve the rank of closeness, nearness and special favour, and observe his station against the slightest disturbance or severance. Because of the intensity of care for him, the increase of His nearness to him, His taking him for Himself, and His choosing him over others, the rights of His friend and Master over him are more complete, His blessings upon him are more perfect, and what is demanded of him is greater than what is demanded of others. So if he becomes heedless and falls short of what his rank requires, he is alerted in a way that the distant outsider is not alerted, while at the same time he is forgiven what that outsider would not be forgiven. Thus both matters come together in his case.

If you wish to know how these two come together without contradiction, reality bears witness to it. A king pardons his close associates and friends in what he would not pardon in one who is not of their rank, and he seizes them and disciplines them for what he does not seize others for. We have mentioned examples of this and that, and there is no contradiction between the two matters.

And if you have two slaves, or two sons, or two wives, one of whom is more beloved to you, closer to your heart, and dearer to you, you treat him with both of these matters, and the two kinds of treatment come together in his case according to his nearness to you, your love for him, and his dearness to you. When you consider the perfection of your kindness to him and the completion of your blessing upon him, his treatment requires that you address him in ways you do not address anyone else, by alerting him and not neglecting him. And when you consider his excellence, his love for you, his obedience and service, and the perfection of his servitude, sincere counsel, and devotion, you forgive him, pardon him and excuse him in ways you do not do with others. So the two kinds of treatment follow what comes from you and what comes from him.

This meaning has been shown to be taken into account in the Sharia, for it made the punishment for one who has been favoured with marriage and then commits adultery stoning, while the punishment for one who has not been given this blessing is flogging. Likewise, it doubled the punishment for the free person who has been granted ownership of himself, whose blessing has been completed and who has not been made the property of another, and it made the punishment for the slave, whose condition is diminished by slavery and who has not received this blessing, half of that.

Glory be to Him, whose wisdom in His creation, His command and His recompense has dazzled the minds of all the worlds, and whose wisdom testifies that He is the Most Wise of judges.

*Verse of poetry:*
> For Allah there is a secret beneath every subtlety,
> and the one of insight dives deep, seeking to gain it.

**[Section]**

Nearness to the Imam has an effect on the secret of prayer, and this nearness has a particular effect on the dawn prayer, which is known to one who understands His saying: ﴿And the recitation of dawn; indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed﴾.

It was said: It is witnessed by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His angels.

And it was said: It is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day, so that the descent of these replacements coincides with the ascent of those, and they gather at the dawn prayer. That is because it is the first register of the day and the last register of the night, so the angels of the night and the day witness it.

Those who held this view argued with what is in the Sahih from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The virtue of the congregational prayer over the prayer of one person is twenty-five degrees."

And the angels of the night and the angels of the day gather at the dawn prayer, according to Abu Hurairah's saying: "Recite if you wish: ﴿And the recitation of dawn; indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed﴾" [al-Isra: 78].

Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Sahih.

The proponents of the first view said: This does not contradict our statement, which is that Allah, glorified is He, and the angels of the night and the day witness the recitation of dawn. The intended meaning is not general witnessing, for Allah is a witness over everything, but a particular witnessing, namely the witnessing of presence and closeness, linked to the nearness of the Lord, exalted is He, and His descent to the lowest heaven in the last third of the night.

Al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated: Ziyadah ibn Muhammad told me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Fadalah ibn Ubayd al-Ansari, from Abu al-Darda, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said:

"Allah, Mighty and Majestic, descends during three hours that remain of the night. In the first hour He opens the Remembrance (*al-Dhikr*) which no one but Him sees, so Allah erases what He wills and establishes. Then in the second hour He descends to the Garden of Eden, which is His abode that no eye has seen and that has not occurred to the heart of any human; it is His dwelling, and no one of the children of Adam dwells with Him there except three: the prophets, the truthful ones and the martyrs. Then He says: 'Blessed is the one who has entered you.' Then in the third hour He descends to the lowest heaven with His spirit and His angels, and He says: 'Stand up, by My might,' and then He looks down upon His servants and says: 'Is there any seeker of forgiveness that I may forgive him? Is there any petitioner who asks Me that I may give him? Is there any supplicant who calls upon Me that I may answer him?' until the dawn prayer."

And for this reason Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And the recitation of dawn; indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed﴾, which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, witnesses, and His angels, the angels of the night and the day, witness.

In this hadith, the descent continues until the dawn prayer. On this basis, Allah's witnessing of the recitation of dawn is together with the witnessing of the angels of the night and the day. This is particular to the dawn prayer and is not shared by other prayers. This does not contradict the continuation of the descent in the other hadiths until the rising of dawn, especially since it is conditioned in some of them upon the breaking of dawn, which is the spreading of its light.

And in one wording: "until the dawn shines," and in another wording: "until the dawn spreads its light."

That is the time for the recitation of the dawn prayer, and this is evidence for the recommendation of performing it early, together with the constant practice of the Prophet ﷺ and his rightly-guided successors of performing it at the beginning of its time. The Prophet ﷺ would recite in it sixty to a hundred verses, lengthen its bowing and prostration, and finish from it while the women could not be recognized because of the darkness (*ghalas*). This would not occur except with great earliness at the beginning of the time, so that the recitation falls in the time of the descent, and the particular witnessing takes place. Moreover, a hadith has come explicitly stating the continuation of this until the conclusion of the dawn prayer. Al-Daraqutni narrated it in his book "The Descent of the Lord, Exalted is He, Every Night to the Lowest Heaven," from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, descends to the lowest heaven for the last half of the night or the last third, and says: 'Who is calling upon Me that I may answer him? Who is asking Me that I may give him? Who is seeking forgiveness from Me that I may forgive him?' until the dawn rises, or the reciter finishes the dawn prayer."

Many have narrated this from Muhammad [ibn Amr], among them Sulayman ibn Bilal, Isma'il ibn Ja'far, al-Darawardi, Hafs ibn Ghiyath, Yazid ibn Harun, Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata, Muhammad ibn Ja'far, and al-Nadr ibn Shumayl; all of them said: "or the reciter finishes the dawn prayer." If this wording is preserved from the Prophet ﷺ, it is explicit in meaning and reveals the intended sense. If it is not preserved, and it was from the doubt of the narrator as to whether he said this or that, then we have already stated that there is no conflict between the two wordings.

The hadith of al-Layth ibn Sa'd from Muhammad ibn Ziyad indicates the continuation of the descent until the time of the dawn prayer, and that its linking to the rising [of dawn] is because it is the first time in which the ascent occurs. This is as narrated by Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq, from his father, from al-Aghurr Abu Muslim, who said: "I bear witness upon the Prophet ﷺ that he said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, delays until, when a third of the night has passed, He descends to this heaven. Then He commands the gates of the heaven, and they are opened. Then He says: Is there anyone asking, that I may give him? Is there anyone calling, that I may answer him? Is there anyone seeking forgiveness, that I may forgive him? Is there anyone seeking relief, that I may relieve him? Is there anyone in distress, that I may remove it from him? He remains in that station until the dawn rises every night in the world, and then He ascends to the heaven.'"

Al-Daraqutni said: Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq added a good addition to it. The purpose of mentioning nearness to the Imam in the dawn prayer and the early performance of it at the beginning of its time is this. And Allah knows best.

(Benefit)

The saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Those who curse much will not be intercessors or witnesses on the Day of Resurrection."

Cursing is an evil act, indeed among the most severe forms of evil, whereas intercession is a form of goodness. Whoever does evil in this world through cursing, God deprives of goodness in the Hereafter through intercession, for a person only reaps what he sows. Evil prevents one from intercession, which is a form of goodness.

As for the prohibition of cursing from being a witness, cursing is enmity, and enmity is incompatible with bearing witness. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ was the master of intercessors and the intercessor of all creation, owing to the perfection of his goodness, compassion and mercy toward them.

[Section: His ﷺ practice regarding the night prayer (qiyam al-layl)]

The early generations (al-salaf) and later scholars (al-khalaf) differed over whether it was obligatory for him or not. Both groups argued from the words of God, Exalted is He: ﴿And from the night, pray with it as a supererogatory act for you﴾.

Those who held that it was not obligatory said: this is explicit in indicating non-obligation. The others said: He commanded him to perform tahajjud in this surah, just as He commanded him in His words: ﴿O you who are wrapped up, rise [to pray] the night, except a little﴾ [al-Muzzammil 73:1–2].

Nothing abrogated this command (naskh) for him. As for His words ﴿as a supererogatory act for you﴾: if nafilah were meant as voluntary worship, He would not have singled him out by saying it is nafilah for him. What is meant by nafilah is an addition (ziyadah), and mere addition does not indicate voluntariness. God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an addition (nafilah)﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:72], meaning an addition beyond the child. Similarly, the nafilah in the Prophet's ﷺ tahajjud is an addition to his ranks and to his reward. This is why He singled him out with it, for qiyam al-layl for others is permissible and expiates sins, whereas the Prophet ﷺ had God forgive him his earlier and later sins, so for him it works toward raising his ranks and elevating his stations, while for others it works toward expiation.

Mujahid said: It was a nafilah for the Prophet ﷺ because his earlier and later sins had been forgiven, so his worship was a nafilah, meaning an addition to reward, whereas for others it is an expiation for their sins. Ibn al-Mundhir said in his tafsir: Yala ibn Abi Ubayd narrated to us, al-Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abdullah ibn Kathir, from Mujahid, who said: Whatever is beyond the obligatory prayer is a nafilah, because it does not work toward expiating sins; there are no nawafil for people, rather they are for the Prophet ﷺ alone, while all people perform what is beyond the obligatory prayer to expiate their sins.

Muhammad ibn Nasr narrated to us, Abdullah narrated to us, Amr narrated to us, from Sa'id and Qabisah, from Sufyan, from Abu Uthman, from al-Hasan regarding the words of God, Exalted is He: ﴿And from the night, pray with it as a supererogatory act for you﴾.

He said: (The nafilah of the night is only for the Prophet ﷺ.)

It is also mentioned from al-Dahhak, who said: a nafilah for the Prophet ﷺ alone.

Sulaym ibn Hayyan mentioned: Abu Ghalib narrated to us, Abu Umamah narrated to us, who said: When you place the ablution in its proper places and rise, you rise forgiven. If you rise to pray, it will be a virtue and a reward for you. A man said: O Abu Umamah, what if someone rises to pray, is it a nafilah for him? He said: No, the nafilah is only for the Prophet ﷺ. How could it be a nafilah for him when he is striving in sins and errors?! It is a virtue and a reward for him.

I say: The intended meaning is that nafilah in the verse does not refer to what may be done or left, like the recommended (mustahabb) and the commendable (mandub); rather, what is meant is the increase in ranks. This is a shared quality between the obligatory and the recommended, so his words "as a supererogatory act for you" do not negate what the command indicates of obligation. A fuller explanation of this issue will come, God willing, when mentioning the special characteristics (khasa'is) of the Prophet ﷺ.

He ﷺ never abandoned the night prayer, whether at home or while travelling. When sleep or pain overcame him, he would pray twelve rak'ahs during the day. I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah say: In this is evidence that witr is not made up (qada') once its time has passed; it is like the greeting prayer of the mosque (tahiyyat al-masjid) and the eclipse prayer and the rain prayer (istisqa') and the like, because its purpose is that the last prayer of the night be witr, just as maghrib is the last prayer of the day. When the night ends and you have prayed subh, witr has not fallen into its proper place. This is the meaning of his words.

Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever sleeps through witr or forgets it, let him pray it when he wakes or remembers." But this hadith has several defects (ilal).

The first: it is from the narration of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, who is weak.

The second: the correct version of it is that it is mursal from him, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ. al-Tirmidhi said: This is more correct, meaning the mursal version.

The third: Ibn Majah related from Muhammad ibn Yahya, after narrating the hadith of Abu Sa'id: The correct version is that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Perform witr before you reach the morning." He said: This hadith is evidence that the hadith of Abd al-Rahman is weak.

The Prophet's ﷺ night prayer was eleven rak'ahs, or thirteen, as Ibn Abbas and Aisha said, for both of these are authentically reported from them. In the two Sahihs (al-Sahihayn) from her: "The Messenger of God ﷺ did not exceed eleven rak'ahs in Ramadan or otherwise."

Also in the two Sahihs from her: "The Messenger of God ﷺ used to pray thirteen rak'ahs at night, making witr with five of them, sitting only at the end of them."

The correct report from Aisha is the first; and the two rak'ahs beyond the eleven are the two rak'ahs of Fajr. This is explained by her in this very hadith: "The Messenger of God ﷺ used to pray thirteen rak'ahs with the two rak'ahs of Fajr," mentioned by Muslim in his Sahih. al-Bukhari said in this hadith: "The Messenger of God ﷺ used to pray thirteen rak'ahs at night, then when he heard the call for Fajr he would pray two light rak'ahs." In the two Sahihs from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, who said: I heard Aisha, may God be pleased with her, say: "The prayer of the Messenger of God ﷺ at night was ten rak'ahs, and he would make witr with one prostration, and he would bow for the two rak'ahs of Fajr, and that makes thirteen rak'ahs." This is explicit and clarified.

(Benefit)

What occurs in Sahih al-Bukhari and most books of hadith is "wa-ib'athhu maqaman mahmudan alladhi wa'adtahu" (and raise him to a praised station which You have promised him).

It occurs in Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah and al-Nasa'i with the chain of the two Sahihs, from the narration of Jabir: "wa-ib'athhu al-maqam al-mahmud" (and raise him to the praised station). Ibn Khuzaymah narrated it from Musa ibn Sahl al-Ramli, whom Abu Hatim al-Razi affirmed as truthful, and the rest of the chain meets their conditions. al-Nasa'i narrated it from Umar ibn Mansur from Ali ibn Abbas. The correct version is what is in al-Bukhari, for the following reasons:

First: most narrators agree on it.

Second: it agrees with the wording of the Qur'an.

Third: the indefinite form in it is intended to exalt it, as in His words: ﴿A Book which We have sent down to you, blessed﴾ and His words: ﴿And this is a blessed remembrance which We have sent down﴾

and His words ﴿And this is a Book confirming﴾ and the like.

Fourth: the definite article would particularize it and restrict it to a specific station, whereas omitting it implies generality and multiplicity, as in His words: ﴿Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter and protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾. His praised stations on the Plain of Judgment are numerous, as the hadiths indicate, so the indefinite carries a generality and broadness that the definite lacks.

Fifth: the Prophet ﷺ was careful to preserve the wording of the Qur'an, in its order, its precedence and postponement, its definiteness and indefiniteness, just as he preserved its meanings.

Among examples of this is his saying, when he began with al-Safa: "I begin with what God began with."

Among examples is his beginning the ablution with the face, then the hands, following the wording of the Qur'an.

Among examples is his saying in the hadith of al-Bara' ibn Azib: "I believed in Your Book which You sent down and Your Prophet whom You sent," in agreement with His words: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you﴾.

Accordingly, "alladhi wa'adtahu" is either a substitute (badal), or the predicate of an omitted subject, or the object of an omitted verb, or an adjective to "maqaman mahmudan," which is close to definite in wording and meaning. Reflect on this.

(Benefit)

Abu Bakr Abd al-Aziz, the servant (ghulam) of al-Khallal, said: I heard some of our shaykhs say: The other prophets refrained from intercession only because they were reproached before forgiveness, so their reluctance kept them from pressing forward. Our Prophet, peace be upon him, was forgiven before any reproach.

(Subtle point)

When the Messenger ﷺ perfected the station of dependence upon God, Glorified is He, he made all creation most in need of Him, in this world and the Hereafter.

As for their need of Him in this world, it is greater than their need for food, drink and the breath by which their bodies live.

As for their need of Him in the Hereafter, they will seek intercession from the prophets before God to relieve them of the distress of their station. All of them will hold back from intercession, until he intercedes for them, and he is the one who opens for them the gate of Paradise.

(Section)

The Messenger of God ﷺ is praised by God, praised by His angels, praised by his brother prophets, praised by all the people of the earth, even if some of them disbelieve in him, for the perfect qualities that are in him are praiseworthy to every sound mind, even if it stubbornly denies them out of rejection, obstinacy or ignorance of his possession of them. Had they known that he possessed them, they would have praised him, for a person praises whoever possesses perfect qualities even if he is unaware of their presence in him; so in reality he is praising him. He ﷺ was singled out, from the meaning of praise, with what was not gathered for anyone else, for his name is Muhammad and Ahmad. His community are the ones who praise much (al-Hammadun), praising God in ease and in hardship. Their prayer begins with praise, their sermon begins with praise, and their book begins with praise. Thus it is with God in the Preserved Tablet, that his successors and companions write the mushaf beginning with praise. In his hand on the Day of Resurrection is the banner of praise, and when he prostrates before his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to intercede, and is permitted to intercede, he will praise his Lord with praises that will be opened for him at that time. He is the possessor of the praised station (al-maqam al-mahmud) which the first and last will envy him for. God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And from the night, pray with it as a supererogatory act for you; perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station﴾, in the sense of the praised station. Let him consider what the early community's Companions and Successors said about it in the commentary of this surah, such as the tafsirs of Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Jarir, Abd ibn Humayd and other tafsirs of the early generations.

When he stands in that station, all the people of the Plain will praise him then, the believer and the disbeliever, the first and the last. He ﷺ is praised for what he filled the earth with of guidance, faith, beneficial knowledge and righteous deeds. Through him God opened hearts, lifted darkness from the people of the earth, and rescued them from the captivity of Satan, from shirk with God, from disbelief in Him and ignorance of Him, until through him his followers attained the honour of this world and the Hereafter. His message reached the people of the earth when they were most in need of it, for they were among worshippers of idols, worshippers of crosses, worshippers of fire, worshippers of the stars, and those who earned God's anger, bewildered, not knowing a Lord to worship nor how to worship Him. People devoured one another; whoever found something good called people to it and fought whoever opposed him. There was no spot on earth that shone with the light of revelation. God, Glorified is He, then looked upon the people of the earth and despised them, Arab and non-Arab, except for remnants following traces of a sound religion. Through him God relieved the lands and their people, lifted those darknesses through him, and gave life to creation after death. Through him He guided from error, taught through him from ignorance, multiplied them after few, exalted them after lowliness, enriched them after poverty, opened through him blind eyes, deaf ears and veiled hearts. So people knew their Lord and their object of worship to the furthest extent their faculties can attain in knowledge. He repeated, abbreviated, and elaborated in mentioning His names, attributes and actions, until His knowledge became manifest in the hearts of His believing servants, and the clouds of doubt and suspicion were lifted from them as clouds part from the moon on the night of its fullness. He left his community no need in this knowledge, neither of anyone before him nor anyone after him; rather it sufficed them, healed them and enriched them from everyone who speaks on this subject. ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book which is recited to them? Indeed in that is mercy and a reminder for a people who believe﴾.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 17, verses 80–81:

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in Makkah, and he was commanded to emigrate, and this was revealed to him: ﴿And say: My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and to exit a sound exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority﴾ [al-Isra: 80]."

Qatadah said: "Allah brought him out from Makkah to Madinah by a sound exit. The Prophet of Allah knew that he had no capacity for this matter except through an authority, so he asked Allah for a supporting authority. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, showed him the abode of emigration while he was in Makkah, and he said: 'I was shown the abode of your emigration: a salt flat with palm trees between two lava plains (lābatayn).'"

(Section)

Allah the Exalted had commanded His Messenger to ask Him to make his entrance and his exit upon truthfulness (ṣidq). He said: ﴿And say: My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and to exit a sound exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority﴾ [al-Isra: 80]. He also told of His intimate friend Ibrahim (ﷺ) that he asked Him to bestow upon him a tongue of truthfulness among the later generations. He said: ﴿And grant me a tongue of truthfulness among the later ones﴾ [al-Shuʿara: 84]. He also gave good news to His servants that they have with Him a footing of truthfulness (qadam ṣidq) and a seat of truthfulness (maqʿad ṣidq). The Exalted said: ﴿And give good news to those who believe that they will have a footing of truthfulness with their Lord﴾ [Yunus: 2], and He said: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and a river, in a seat of truthfulness, in the presence of a Sovereign, Omnipotent﴾ [al-Qamar: 54–55].

So these are five things: the sound entrance, the sound exit, the tongue of truthfulness, the footing of truthfulness, and the seat of truthfulness.

The reality of truthfulness (ṣidq) in these things is: the firm, established truth, connected to Allah, leading to Allah, and consisting of what is done by it and for it, of statements and actions, and its recompense in this world and the Hereafter.

As for the sound entrance and the sound exit: they mean that one's entering and exiting is an established truth through Allah and in pursuit of His pleasure, by attaining the aim and reaching the sought goal. This is the opposite of the false exit and false entrance, which has no end to which it leads, nor a firm footing on which it stands, like the exit of his enemies on the Day of Badr. The sound exit is like his exit (ﷺ) and that of his Companions in that expedition.

Likewise, his (ﷺ) entrance into Madinah was a sound entrance, through Allah, for Allah, and seeking the pleasure of Allah. Thus there was joined to it support, victory, triumph, and the attainment of what he sought in this world and the Hereafter. This is unlike the false entrance which his enemies intended to enter Madinah by on the Day of the Confederates (al-Ahzab), for it was not through Allah nor for Allah, but rather was opposition to Allah and His Messenger, so only abandonment and ruin were joined to it.

Likewise is the entrance of those Jews who fought against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) into the fortress of Banu Qurayzah. When it was a false entrance, what befell them with them befell him too.

So every entrance and exit that is through Allah and for Allah, its doer is a guarantee upon Allah. It is a sound entrance and a sound exit.

Some of the early generations (al-Salaf), when they went out of their house, would raise their head to the sky and say: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from going out on an exit in which I am not a guarantee upon You."

He means: that the exit should not be other than a sound exit. For this reason the sound entrance and exit have been explained as: his (ﷺ) departure from Makkah and his entrance into Madinah. There is no doubt that this is by way of example, for this entrance and exit are among the most noble of his entrances and exits (ﷺ). Otherwise, all his entrances are sound entrances and all his exits are sound exits, since they are for Allah, through Allah, by His command, and seeking His pleasure.

No one leaves his house and enters his market, or any other entrance, except with truthfulness or with falsehood; so the exit and entrance of each person do not exceed truthfulness or falsehood. And Allah is the One sought for help.

As for the tongue of truthfulness: it is the good praise of him (ﷺ) from all nations, based on truth, not praise based on falsehood. As He said concerning Ibrahim and his offspring of the prophets and messengers, upon them be the blessings and peace of Allah: ﴿And We made for them a tongue of truthfulness, exalted﴾ [Maryam: 50]. The meaning of "tongue" here is good praise. Since truthfulness is with the tongue, and it is its locus, Allah, glory be to Him, made the tongues of servants speak praise of the truthful, as a fitting recompense, and expressed it by that.

The word "tongue" (lisan) is used with three meanings: this one, language, and the organ itself. As in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except with the language of his people to make things clear for them﴾ [Ibrahim: 4]; and His saying: ﴿And the differences of your tongues and your colors﴾ [al-Rum: 22]; and His saying: ﴿The tongue of the one they point to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue﴾ [al-Nahl: 103]. It is also used to mean the organ itself, as in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 16].

As for the footing of truthfulness: it has been explained as Paradise, and explained as Muhammad (ﷺ), and explained as the righteous deeds.

The reality of the "footing" is what they sent ahead (qaddamū), and what they will advance upon on the Day of Resurrection. They sent ahead their deeds and their faith in Muhammad (ﷺ), and they will advance upon Paradise, which is the recompense for that.

So whoever explained it as Paradise meant: what they advance upon. And whoever explained it as the deeds and as the Prophet (ﷺ), then that is because they sent them ahead, and they sent ahead their faith in him before them. So all three are a footing of truthfulness.

As for the seat of truthfulness: it is Paradise, in the presence of the Lord, blessed and exalted.

Describing all of that as truthful entails its being established and firm, that it is true, lasting, beneficial, and of complete benefit. For it is connected to the Truth, glory be to Him, existing through Him and for Him. So it is truthful and not false, true and not vain, lasting and not perishing, beneficial and not harmful. Falsehood and its associated matters have no path or entrance to it.

Among the signs of truthfulness is the calm (tumaʾnīnah) of the heart toward it, and among the signs of falsehood is the arising of doubt (rībah), as in al-Tirmidhi, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) through the hadith of al-Hasan ibn ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Truthfulness is tranquility, and falsehood is doubt." And in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. A man will keep speaking the truth until he is written with Allah as a truthful one (siddiq). And falsehood leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire. A man will keep lying until he is written with Allah as a great liar." So he made truthfulness the key to the state of being a siddiq (siddiqiyyah) and its beginning, and it is its ultimate goal. No liar ever attains its rank, not in his speech, nor in his deeds, nor in his state. Especially one who lies about Allah regarding His names and attributes, denying what He affirmed for Himself or affirming what He negated of Himself. There is never a siddiq among these.

Likewise is lying upon Him regarding His religion and His law: by making lawful what He prohibited, prohibiting what He did not prohibit, dropping what He made obligatory, making obligatory what He did not make obligatory, disliking what He loved, and recommending what He did not love. All of this is contrary to siddiqiyyah.

Likewise is lying with Him in deeds: by adorning oneself with the adornment of the truthful sincere ones and the ascetic reliant ones, while not truly being among them.

Therefore siddiqiyyah is the perfection of sincerity, submission, and following the report and the command, outwardly and inwardly, to the extent that the truthfulness of two parties to a sale brings blessing into their sale, and their lying erases the blessing of their sale. As in the two Sahihs, from Hakim ibn Hizam, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The two parties to a sale have the option (of cancellation) as long as they have not separated. If they are truthful and make things clear, their sale is blessed for them. If they lie and conceal, the blessing of their sale is erased."

[The Qur'an is a healing]

Allah, glory be to Him, has informed us about the Qur'an that it is a healing, and Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And if We had made it a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said, "Why have its verses not been explained in detail? Is it non-Arabic and Arabic?" Say, "It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing."﴾ [Fussilat: 44]

And He said: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is healing and mercy for the believers﴾ [al-Isra': 82].

Here, "min" (from) is for explaining the genus (bayan al-jins), not for partitioning (li-l-tab'id), because the whole Qur'an is healing, as He said in the previous verse. It is healing for hearts from the disease of ignorance, doubt and suspicion. Allah, glory be to Him, has not sent down from the sky any healing ever more comprehensive, more beneficial, greater, or more effective in removing disease than the Qur'an.

It is established in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id, who said:

"A group of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ set out on a journey they were making, until they stopped at a tribe of the tribes of the Arabs and asked them for hospitality, but they refused to host them. Then the chief of that tribe was stung, so they tried everything for him, but nothing benefited him. Some of them said: 'If you went to these people who have stopped here, perhaps some of them have something.' So they came to them and said: 'O company, our chief has been stung, and we have tried everything for him, but nothing benefits him. Does any of you have anything?' One of them said: 'By Allah, I do ruqyah, but by Allah, we asked you for hospitality and you did not host us, so I will not perform ruqyah until you give me a reward.' So they agreed with them on a flock of sheep. He set off, blowing over him and reciting ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, and it was as if he had been released from a fetter, and he walked off, with no ailment remaining in him. They gave them the reward they had agreed upon. Some of them said: 'Divide it.' The one who had performed the ruqyah said: 'We will not do so until we come to the Prophet ﷺ and tell him what happened, and see what he orders us.' They came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him about it. He said: 'How did you know that it was a ruqyah?' Then he said: 'You have done well. Divide it, and set aside a share for me with you.'"

So this remedy had an effect on this disease, and removed it until it was as if it had never been. It is the easiest and simplest of remedies. If the servant were to treat himself well with al-Fatihah, he would see a wondrous effect of it in healing.

I stayed in Makkah for a period, and ailments afflicted me, and I found neither a physician nor a medicine, so I treated myself with al-Fatihah, and I saw from it a wondrous effect. I would describe that to whoever complained of pain, and many of them would recover quickly.

But here there is a matter that deserves attention: the remembrances, verses and supplications by which one seeks healing and performs ruqyah are in themselves beneficial and healing, but they require the acceptance of the recipient (qabul al-mahall), the strength of resolve of the one who acts (quwwat himmat al-fa'il) and its influence. Whenever healing fails, it is due either to weakness in the influence of the one acting, or to the recipient not accepting it, or to a strong obstacle in him that prevents the medicine from taking effect in him, just as this occurs with physical medicines and physical diseases. The failure of their effect may be due to the nature not accepting that medicine, or to a strong obstacle preventing it from producing its effect. When the nature takes the medicine with complete acceptance, the body benefits from it in proportion to that acceptance. Likewise, when the heart takes ruqyah and amulets with complete acceptance, and the reciter has a powerful soul and an effective resolve in removing the disease.

And he said in Zad al-Ma'ad:

Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is healing and mercy for the believers﴾

The correct view is that "min" here is for explaining the genus, not for partitioning. And He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿O mankind, there has come to you an admonition from your Lord and a healing for what is in the breasts﴾ [Yunus: 57].

The Qur'an is therefore the complete healing from all diseases of hearts and bodies, and of the disease of this world and the Hereafter. Not everyone is qualified for it or granted success in seeking healing through it. When the patient treats himself with it well, places it on his disease with sincerity, faith, complete acceptance, firm conviction, and fulfilling its conditions, the disease will never overcome it.

How could diseases overcome the speech of the Lord of the earth and the heavens, which, had it descended upon the mountains, would have split them, or upon the earth, would have torn it apart? There is no disease of the hearts or bodies except that in the Qur'an is a way of guidance to its remedy and its cause, and of protection from it for whoever Allah grants understanding of His Book. The introduction to the discussion of medicine earlier explained the guidance of the Mighty Qur'an to its principles and foundations, which are preserving health and protection (al-hima), and expelling what is harmful, and deducing from this the rest of the types of these categories.

As for the remedies of the heart, it mentions them in detail, and mentions the causes of its diseases and their treatment. He said: ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book, which is recited to them?﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 51]. So whoever is not healed by the Qur'an, may Allah not heal him, and whoever is not sufficed by it, may Allah not suffice him.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 17, verse 84 (part 1 of 2):

Shaqiq ibn Ibrahim said: "The door of divine success (tawfiq) is closed to creation for six things: their being occupied with blessings instead of thanking for them; their desire for knowledge while abandoning action; their hastening toward sin; their delaying repentance; their being deluded by the companionship of the righteous while not emulating their deeds; and the world turning its back on them while they pursue it, and the Hereafter turning toward them while they turn away from it."

I say: The root of all this is the absence of desire (raghba) and fear (rahba), and its root is weakness of certainty (yaqin), and its root is weakness of insight (basira), and its root is the baseness and lowliness of the soul, and the exchanging of what is lower for what is better. Otherwise, if the soul were noble and great, it would not be content with the base. So the root of all good is by the success (tawfiq) and will of God, and the nobility, honor and greatness of the soul; and the root of all evil is its meanness, lowliness and smallness. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿He has indeed succeeded who purifies it, and he has failed who buries it﴾ [91:9–10]; that is, whoever makes it great and grows it through obedience to God has succeeded, and whoever makes it small and degraded through disobedience to God has failed. Noble souls are not content with anything except the highest, the best, and the most praiseworthy in its outcome, while base souls hover around lowly things and settle upon them, as flies settle upon filth. A noble, lofty soul is not content with injustice, with indecencies, or with theft and betrayal, for it is greater and more exalted than that. The debased, contemptible, and vile soul is the opposite of this. Thus every soul inclines toward what suits it and resembles it, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Say: Each acts according to his own manner (shakila)﴾ [17:84]; that is, according to what resembles and suits it. He acts according to his way, which fits his character and nature. Every person proceeds according to his path, his doctrine, and the habit he has grown accustomed to and been formed upon. The wicked person acts in a manner resembling his way, by repaying blessings with disobedience and turning away from blessings; the believer acts in a manner that suits him: thanking for blessings, loving Him, praising Him, drawing near to Him in affection, being shy before Him, watching over Him, and magnifying and honoring Him.

(A subtle point)
You trained your dog, and it refrains from its desire to eat what it has caught, out of reverence for your blessing and fear of your power.
How often has the teacher of the Law taught you, while you do not accept?
The hunting of the ignorant one and of the one who keeps for himself is forbidden; so what of the ignorant one whose deeds are for the desire of his soul?
Within you are combined the intellect of an angel, the appetite of a beast, and the desire of Satan.
And you belong to whichever of the three prevails over you.
If your appetite and desire prevail, you rise above the rank of an angel.
And if your desire and appetite overcome you, you fall below the rank of a dog.
When the dog hunts for its master, its game is made lawful.
And when it keeps for itself, what it has caught is forbidden.

(Section: Each person's pleasure is according to his capacity, his aspiration, and the nobility of his soul)
The most noble of people in soul, the highest in aspiration, and the most elevated in rank find their pleasure in knowing God, loving Him, longing to meet Him, and drawing near to Him with what He loves and is pleased with. Their pleasure lies in turning toward Him and their aspiration being devoted to Him. Below this are levels that none can count except God, until one reaches the person whose pleasure lies in the basest things, in filth and indecencies, in every kind of speech, action, and occupation. If what the first one takes pleasure in were presented to him, his soul would not permit him to accept it or even to turn toward it, and it may even cause him pain; just as, if what the second takes pleasure in were presented to the first, his soul would not permit it, would not turn toward it, and would recoil from it. The most complete people in pleasure are those for whom is combined the pleasure of the heart and spirit with the pleasure of the body: they enjoy lawful pleasures in a manner that does not diminish their share of this world and the Hereafter, and that does not cut off from them the pleasure of knowing, loving, and being intimate with their Lord. Of such people God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He brought forth for His servants, and the good provisions? Say: They are for those who believed in the life of this world, purely for them on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [7:32]. The one with the least share of pleasure is the one who enjoys these things in a manner that comes between him and the pleasures of the Hereafter, so that he becomes one of those to whom it will be said on the Day of enjoyment: ﴿You squandered your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them﴾ [46:20]. Both groups enjoyed good things, but they differed in the manner of enjoyment. The first enjoyed them in the way He permitted for them, so their pleasure of this world and of the Hereafter was combined. The second enjoyed them in the way desire and appetite led them, whether or not He permitted it; so the pleasure of this world was cut off from them and the pleasure of the Hereafter escaped them. Neither the pleasure of this world remained with them, nor was the pleasure of the Hereafter attained by them. Whoever loves pleasure, its lasting, and a good life, let him make the pleasure of this world a means to the pleasure of the next, by seeking help from it to empty his heart for God, to direct his will and worship to Him, taking it by the measure of seeking aid and strength for His pursuit, not by the measure of mere appetite and desire. And if he is one from whom the pleasures and good things of this world have been withheld, let him make whatever has been lost from them an increase in the pleasure of the Hereafter, and let him restrain his soul here through abstention in order to receive them in full there. The good things and pleasures of this world are an excellent aid to one whose quest is sincerely for God and the Hereafter and whose aspiration is for what is there; and they are a wretched obstacle to one for whom they are the ultimate aim and aspiration, around which he revolves. Their loss in this world is an excellent aid to the seeker of God and the Hereafter, and a wretched obstacle and deprivation from God and the Hereafter. Whoever takes the benefits of this world in a manner that does not diminish his share of the Hereafter attains both together; otherwise he loses both together.

Glory be to God, Lord of the worlds! Even if there were in abandoning sins and transgressions nothing but the upholding of manliness (muruwwa), the preservation of honor, the safeguarding of standing, the protection of wealth which God made a support for the interests of this world and the Hereafter, love among people, good speech among them, the goodness of livelihood, ease of body, strength of heart, contentment of soul, delight of the heart, expansion of the breast, security from the fears of the wicked and the sinners, lessening of worry, grief, and sorrow, the might of the soul in refusing humiliation, the preservation of the light of the heart from being extinguished by the darkness of disobedience, the attainment of a way out from what has constricted upon the wicked and the sinners, the facilitation of provision from where he does not expect, the easing of what is difficult for the people of sin and transgression, the making of acts of obedience easy for him, the facilitation of knowledge, a good reputation among people, many prayers for him, the sweetness that appears in his face, the awe that is cast into people's hearts for him, their support and zeal for him when he is harmed or wronged, their defense of his honor when a backbiter slanders him, the swiftness of the answering of his supplication, the removal of the estrangement between him and God, the nearness of the angels to him, the distance of the devils of mankind and jinn from him, people's competition in serving him and fulfilling his needs, their seeking his friendship and companionship, his not fearing death but rejoicing in it for the sake of coming to his Lord, meeting Him and returning to Him, the worldly life being small in his heart and the Hereafter great in his sight, his eagerness for the great kingdom and the mighty triumph there, his tasting the sweetness of obedience and finding the sweetness of faith, the supplication for him by the bearers of the Throne and those around it of the angels, the joy of the recording angels in him and their prayers for him at all times, an increase in his intellect, understanding, faith and knowledge, the love of God for him being attained, His turning toward him, and His joy at his repentance, and thus He recompenses him with a joy and delight that has no comparison to his joy and delight in disobedience in any respect.

These are some of the effects of abandoning sins in this world. When he dies, the angels meet him with the good news from his Lord of Paradise and that no fear and no grief shall be upon him, and he is transferred from the prison of this world and its narrowness to a meadow of the gardens of Paradise, where he enjoys until the Day of Resurrection. When the Day of Resurrection comes, people will be in the heat and sweat while he is in the shade of the Throne. When they disperse from before God, he will be taken to the right hand together with His friends, the righteous, and His party, the successful. ﴿That is the bounty of God, which He gives to whom He wills, and God is Possessor of great bounty.﴾

[Section defining will (irada)]
The author of "al-Manazil" (may God have mercy on him) said:
Chapter on will (al-irada): God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: Each acts according to his own manner﴾ [al-Isra: 84].
In his opening the chapter with this verse is an indication of the greatness of its rank and the magnitude of its place in this science. The meaning of the verse is: each acts according to everything that resembles him, suits him, and befits him. The wicked person acts according to what befits him. Likewise the unbeliever, the hypocrite, and the one who desires this world and its carrion acts according to what suits him and does not befit anything else. The lover of forms acts according to what suits him and befits him.
So every person yearns toward what he loves, and every person inclines toward what suits him. The sincere seeker of will, the lover of God, does what is most fitting and suitable for him. He acts according to the manner of his will, and according to what is most fitting for it and most proper to it.
He said: Will is among the laws of this science and the comprehensive foundations of its structures, and it is the responding to the calls of reality, willingly or unwillingly.
He means: this science is built upon will; it is its foundation and the gathering point of its structure. It encompasses the details of the rulings of will, which is the movement of the heart. For this reason it is called the science of the inner (batin), just as the science of jurisprudence (fiqh) encompasses the details of the rulings of the limbs, and for this reason it is called the science of the outer (zahir).
These are two voluntary movements, while the servant also has a natural, involuntary movement. The science that encompasses its details and rulings is the science of medicine (tibb). These three sciences are the ones that enable knowledge of the movements of the soul and the heart, the movements of the tongue and limbs, and the movements of nature.
The physician examines these movements from the standpoint of their effect on the body, in health and sickness, and in their consequences and connections.
The jurist examines these movements from the standpoint of their conformity with the command, prohibition, permission, and disapproval of the Law, and what is connected to these.
The Sufi examines these movements from the standpoint of whether they lead him to his goal, or cut him off from it and corrupt his heart, or correct it.
As for his saying: "It is the responding to the call of reality": responding is submission and compliance. Reality, in their view, is witnessing lordship (rububiyya); and the Law is the commitment to servanthood (ubudiyya).
So the Law is that you worship Him; and reality is that you witness Him.
The Law is your standing by His command; reality is your witnessing of His attribute. The call of reality is the soundness of knowledge, for whoever knows God loves Him without fail.
In this response there must be three things: a soul prepared and receptive, which lacks only the caller; a call that is heard; and the clearing of the path from obstacles.
Whoever is cut off is cut off only from one of these three directions.
His saying "willingly or unwillingly" points to the one drawn in (majdhub), snatched away from himself, and the one who travels with will, choice, and striving.

(Benefit)
Among people there is one whose chief work and path, which he considers his journey to God, is the path of knowledge and teaching. He has cleared his time for it, seeking the face of God, and he continues thus, devoted to the path of knowledge and teaching, until through that path he reaches God and a special opening is granted him in it, or he dies on the path of his seeking, and it is hoped that he will attain his goal after death.
God, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever leaves his home emigrating to God and His Messenger, then death overtakes him, his reward has indeed fallen upon God﴾ [al-Nisa: 100].
It has been related from a large group of those whom death overtook while they were eagerly seeking the Qur'an that they were seen after their death and informed that they were completing their pursuit and learning in the barzakh, for a servant dies upon what he lived upon.
Among people there is one whose chief work is remembrance (dhikr), which he has made his provision for his return and the capital for his destination; whenever he slackens in it or falls short, he sees himself as having been defrauded and having lost. Among people there is one whose chief work and path is prayer; whenever he falls short in his portion of it, or a time passes while he is not occupied with it or prepared for it, his time grows dark for him and his breast is constricted.
Among people there is one whose path is kindness and beneficial service to others, such as meeting needs, relieving distresses, aiding those in distress, and various kinds of charity; an opening has been granted him in this, and he has traveled by it to his Lord. Among people there is one whose path is recitation of the Qur'an, which dominates his times, and it is the greatest of his litanies. Among people there is one whose path is fasting; whenever he breaks his fast, his heart changes and his condition worsens.
Among them is one whose path is commanding good and forbidding evil; God has granted him an opening in it, and through it he has reached his Lord. Among them is one whose path through which he passes is the pilgrimage and the minor pilgrimage. Among them is one whose path is cutting off attachments, concentrating his aspiration, constant watchfulness, observing the movements of the heart, and guarding the hours from being wasted.
Among them is one who gathers together the wayfarer toward God in every valley and the one who arrives at Him by every road. He has made the duties of his servanthood the qibla of his heart and the object before his eyes, which he faces wherever it is and travels with wherever it goes. He has struck with an arrow from every group: wherever servanthood is, you will find him there. If it is knowledge, you find him with its people; if it is jihad, you find him in the ranks of the fighters; if it is prayer, you find him among the devout; if it is remembrance, you find him among the remembrancers; if it is kindness and benefit, you find him in the company of the good-doers; or watchfulness, love, and turning in repentance to God, you find him in the company of those who love and repent. He follows the religion of servanthood wherever its mounts journey and turns toward it wherever its tents are pitched. If he were asked: What do you want of the deeds? He would say: I want to carry out the commands of my Lord wherever they are and wherever they may be, bringing what they bring and requiring what they require, whether they unite or divide, having no aim but to carry them out and to perform them, watched over by Him in them, devoted to Him with spirit, heart, body and inner self, having delivered the sale to Him and awaiting from Him the delivery of the price: ﴿Indeed God has purchased from the believers their selves and their wealth, for them is Paradise﴾ [al-Tawba: 111]. This is the servant who travels to his Lord and arrives at Him in truth.
The meaning of arriving at Him is that his heart is connected to Him and is attached to Him with the attachment of the perfect lover to his beloved, so that he is consoled by Him from all other aims, and nothing remains in his heart but the love of God, His command, and the seeking of nearness to Him.

When the servant walks this path, his Lord turns toward him, draws him near, chooses him, takes his heart to Himself, and takes charge of all his affairs, in his livelihood and his religion. He cares for him in a way more excellent and complete than a compassionate father cares for his child. He, glory be to Him, is the Self-Subsisting, who sustains every created thing, the obedient and the disobedient alike. How, then, will His sustaining care be for one whom He loves, whom He takes as His own, whom He prefers over all others, and whom He accepts from among people as a beloved, a lord, a protector, a helper, a supporter, and a guide? If the veil were lifted from His gentle kindness, His goodness, and His making for him, from what he knows and from what he does not know, his heart would melt with love for Him and longing for Him, and would fall into gratitude to Him. But the hearts are veiled from witnessing this because they cling to the world of desires and attach themselves to means, so they are turned away from the perfection of their bliss. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.

Otherwise, what heart tastes the sweetness of knowing God and loving Him, and then inclines to other than Him and settles in something besides Him?

This never happens. Whoever has tasted something of that, and has known a path leading to God, and then abandoned it and turned toward his own will, comforts, desires, pleasures, and appetites, falls into the traces of ruin. He lodges his heart in the prisons of narrow straits and is tormented in his life with a torment that no one among the worlds has suffered. His life is helplessness, grief, and sorrow; his death is turbidity and regret; his return is sorrow and remorse. His affair is lost to him, and his unity is scattered. His soul brings before him distress and sadness. He has neither the pleasure of the ignorant nor the ease of the knowers. He cries for help but is not helped, and he complains but is not heeded. His joys and gladness have departed, turning their backs, while his pains, sorrows, and regrets have come forward. His intimacy has been replaced by estrangement, his might by humiliation, his wealth by poverty, and his togetherness by dispersion. They have pushed him away, so he does not attain nearness to them, and in place of intimacy they have given him alienation. That is because he knew the way to God and then abandoned it, turning away from it and falling on his face. He saw, then became blind; he knew, then denied; he advanced, then retreated; he was called, but did not answer; the door was opened for him, but he turned his back to it. He has abandoned the path of his Master and turned wholly toward his own desire. If he attains some of his portions and takes pleasure in his comforts and affairs, his heart is still bound, unable to be freed into the vast expanse of divine unity (tawhid), the fields of intimacy, the gardens of love, and the tables of nearness. Through his turning away from his true God he has fallen to the lowest of the low and has entered the ranks of the lost. The fire of the veil rises over his heart at every moment, and the turning away of the created world from him, since he turned away from his Lord, stands between him and his desire. He is a grave walking upon the face of the earth: his spirit is in estrangement from his body, and his heart is in weariness of his life. He wishes for death and longs for it, even though it contains what it contains. Then, when death comes to him in that state, may God protect us, you cannot ask about the painful torment that befalls him, because of the veil that has fallen between him and his true Master, and because the fire of distance from His nearness and turning away from Him encircles him, and he has been prevented from his happiness and his hope.

If the poor servant were to imagine this state, and his own soul were to show it to him as it truly is, his heart would be torn apart, by God, and he would take no pleasure in food or drink. He would go out to open ground, crying out to God, seeking help from Him, and asking Him to be pleased with him in the time of seeking to be pleased. This is so even though, when he prefers his fleeting desires and pleasures, which are like the image of a phantom or a summer cloud, their delights become bitter to him at the moment he most needs them, and he is prevented from them at the moment he is most able to enjoy them. That is God's way with His creation, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Until, when the earth took its adornment and was beautified, and its people thought they had power over it, Our command came to it by night or by day, and We made it a harvest as if it had not flourished yesterday. Thus We detail the signs for a people who give thought.﴾

[Section: Whether the soul is eternal or created and originated]

The question is: is the soul eternal, or is it originated and created? If it is created and originated, and it is from the command of Allah, then how can the command of Allah be originated and created? Allah, glory be to Him, has informed that He breathed into Adam of His soul. Does this attribution to Him indicate that it is eternal or not?

What is the reality of this attribution?

He has informed concerning Adam that He created him with His hand and breathed into him of His soul. Did He attribute the hand and the soul to Himself in the same manner?

This is a question in which a scholar slipped and in which groups of the children of Adam went astray. Allah guided the followers of His Messenger in it to the manifest truth and the clear correctness. The Messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, unanimously agreed that it is originated, created, made, nurtured and managed. This is known by necessity from the religion of the Messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, just as it is known by necessity from their religion that the world is originated, that the resurrection of bodies will occur, and that Allah alone is the Creator, and everything other than Him is created by Him. The era of the Companions, the Successors and the Successors of the Successors, who are the virtuous generations, passed upon this without any disagreement among them concerning its origination and that it is created. Then there arose a person whose understanding of the Book and the Sunnah was deficient, who claimed that it is eternal and uncreated, and argued that it is from the command of Allah, and His command is uncreated, and that Allah, exalted is He, attributed it to Himself just as He attributed to Himself His knowledge, His Book, His power, His hearing, His sight and His hand. Others hesitated and said: we do not say it is created nor that it is uncreated.

The memorizer of Isfahan, Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Mandah, was asked about this. He said: As for what follows, a questioner asked me about the soul which Allah, glory be to Him, made the sustainer of the selves and bodies of creation, and he mentioned groups who spoke about the soul and claimed that it is uncreated, and some of them singled out from it the spirits of holiness and said they are from the essence of Allah. He said: I will mention the differing statements of their predecessors, and I will make clear what contradicts their statements from the Book and the reports, and I will clarify the error of the one who speaks about the soul without knowledge, and that their speech agrees with the view of Jahm and his companions.

We say, and success is from Allah:

People have differed in knowing the spirits and their place in the self.

1. Some of them said: the spirits are all created. This is the doctrine of the People of the Community (Ahl al-Jama'ah) and of the reports (al-athar). They argued with the saying of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace: "The spirits are armies mobilized; whatever recognizes itself among them is united, and whatever is incompatible among them is divided."

Mobilized armies cannot be anything but created.

2. Some of them said: the spirits are from the command of Allah; Allah concealed their reality and knowledge from creation. They argued with the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿Say: the spirit is of the command of my Lord﴾.

3. Some of them said: the spirits are a light from the light of Allah, exalted is He, and a life from His life. They argued with the saying of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace: "Indeed Allah created His creation in darkness, then cast upon them some of His light."

Then he mentioned the disagreement concerning the spirits: whether they die or not, whether they are punished along with the bodies in the barzakh and in their abode after death, and whether they are the self or something other than it.

4. Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi said in his book: a category of heretics (zanadiqa) and a category of Rafidites interpreted the spirit of Adam as the Christians interpreted the spirit of Jesus, and as some people interpreted that the spirit separated from the essence of Allah and came to be in the believer; so a category of Christians worshipped Jesus and Mary together, because Jesus, in their view, is a spirit from Allah that came to be in Mary, so he is uncreated in their view.

5. A category of heretics and a category of Rafidites said: the spirit of Adam is likewise, that it is uncreated. They interpreted the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And I breathed into him of My spirit﴾, and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then He fashioned him and breathed into him of His spirit﴾, and they claimed that the spirit of Adam is not created, just as the one who said that the light from the Lord is uncreated interpreted it. He said: Then after Adam they came to be in the successor after him, then in every prophet and successor, until it came to be in 'Ali, then in al-Hasan and al-Husayn, then in every successor and imam, in whom the imam knows everything and does not need to learn from anyone.

There is no disagreement among the Muslims that the spirits which are in Adam, his descendants, Jesus, and everyone else among the children of Adam are all created by Allah: He created them, brought them into being, originated them and invented them, then attributed them to Himself as He attributed to Himself the rest of His creation. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And He subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all of it from Him﴾.

6. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said: the spirit of the human being is created and originated, by the agreement of the salaf of the community, its imams, and all the people of the Sunnah.

Several of the imams of the Muslims have related the consensus of the scholars that it is created, such as Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi, the well-known imam who, by consensus, was among the most knowledgeable people of his time regarding consensus and disagreement. Likewise Abu Muhammad ibn Qutaybah, who said in (Kitab al-Lafz), when he spoke about the spirit: "al-nasam" are the spirits. He said: The people have agreed that Allah, exalted is He, is the Creator of the grain and the Originator of the breath (nasmah), that is, the Creator of the spirit.

Abu Ishaq ibn Shaqla said in what he answered on this question: "You asked, may Allah have mercy on you, whether the spirit is created or uncreated?" He said: This is something about which no one who has been granted success to the truth doubts, or the spirit is among created things. Groups of great scholars and shaykhs have spoken on this question and refuted those who claim it is uncreated. The memorizer Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Mandah wrote a large book on it; before him Imam Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi and others did so, and Shaykh Abu Sa'id al-Kharraz, Abu Ya'qub al-Nahrajuri, and the qadi Abu Ya'la.

The great imams have explicitly stated this, and their denunciation of anyone who says this about the spirit of Jesus son of Mary was severe; so how about the spirit of anyone else?

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 17, verse 110:

As for the words of the Exalted: ﴿Say: Call upon Allah, or call upon the Most Merciful; whichever you call upon, to Him belong the most beautiful names﴾

This is the well-known explanation, and it is that this calling is the calling of request (du'a' al-mas'alah), and it is the occasion of revelation. They said: "The Prophet ﷺ used to call upon his Lord, saying once, 'O Allah,' and once, 'O Most Merciful,' so the ignorant among the polytheists thought that he was calling upon two gods, and so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "The polytheists heard the Prophet ﷺ calling in his prostration, 'O Most Merciful, O Most Compassionate,' and they said: 'This one claims to call upon one God, yet he calls upon two, two by two.' So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿Say: Call upon Allah, or call upon the Most Merciful﴾."

It has also been said that the calling (du'a') here means naming (tasmiyah), like the saying of people: "I called my son Sa'id," and "Call him 'Abd Allah," and the like. The meaning would then be: Name Allah, or name the Most Merciful. So the calling here means naming. This is the view of al-Zamakhshari, and what led him to this view is the words: ﴿whichever you call upon, to Him belong the most beautiful names﴾, for the intended meaning of "whichever" (ayyan) and its generality here is only the multiplicity of names. The meaning is: whatever name you name Him by from the names of Allah the Exalted, whether Allah or the Most Merciful, to Him belong the most beautiful names; that is, to the One named, glory be to Him, belong the most beautiful names. The pronoun in (lahu) refers to the One named. This is what compelled him to take the calling in this verse to mean naming. But what he said is a necessary implication of the meaning intended by "calling" in the verse, and it is not its exact meaning. Rather, the intended meaning of calling is its known sense, consistently used in the Qur'an, which is the calling of request and the calling of praise, but it includes the meaning of naming. So the intended meaning is not mere naming free of worship and petition, but the naming that occurs within the calling of praise and petition. On this understanding, it is valid that (tad'u) carries the meaning of (tusammu), so reflect on this. The meaning is: whichever you name Him in your praise, your calling, and your request. And Allah knows best.

[Section: The wisdom in distinguishing, in describing, between the night prayer and the day prayer]

As for the distinction between the night prayer and the day prayer in audible and silent recitation, it is in the utmost appropriateness and wisdom. For the night is the setting of the quieting of voices, the stillness of movements, the emptiness of hearts, and the gathering of resolves that are scattered by day. The day is the place of long glorifying with the heart and body, while the night is the place of the heart's agreement with the tongue and the tongue's agreement with the ear. For this reason the Sunnah was to lengthen the recitation in the dawn prayer over the other prayers, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would recite in it from sixty to a hundred verses, and al-Siddiq would recite in it al-Baqarah, and 'Umar would recite al-Nahl, Hud, Bani Isra'il, Yunus and similar surahs; because the heart is at its most free of preoccupations when it awakens from sleep. So when the first thing that strikes his hearing is the speech of Allah, in which is all good in its entirety, it meets him free of preoccupations, and so it settles in him without competition. As for the day, since it is the opposite of that, the recitation of its prayer was silent, unless some stronger overriding matter arises, such as the great gatherings of the two festivals, Friday, the rain prayer, and the eclipse; for then audibility is better and more effective in achieving the purpose, more beneficial for gathering, and in it is the recitation of Allah's speech to them and its delivery in the great gatherings, which is among the greatest aims of the Message. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 17, verse 111:

He, glory be to Him, does not take as a close ally (yuwali) one who seeks allies from among humiliation, as a created being takes an ally among created beings. Rather, He takes as allies His friends (awliya') out of beneficence, mercy and love for them. As for the servants, as the Mighty and Majestic One said: ﴿And Allah is the Rich, while you are the poor﴾ [Muhammad: 38].

Because of their poverty and need, some of them show kindness to others only out of their need for that and their benefit from it, whether in this world or the next. Had they not imagined that benefit, they would not have shown kindness to him. Thus, in reality, he intends kindness to himself, and makes his kindness to others a means and a path by which the benefit of that kindness reaches him. For he either shows kindness to him in anticipation of his reward in this world, since he is in need of that reward, or as an exchange for his kindness, or in anticipation of his praise and gratitude. He also shows kindness to him so that he obtains from him what he needs of commendation and praise, so he is being kind to himself by being kind to others. Or he intends a reward from Allah, exalted is He, in the Hereafter; he too is being kind to himself by that, and he has only postponed his reward until the day of his poverty and dire need. He is not blameworthy in this intention, for he is poor and needy, and his poverty and need are a necessary attribute of his essence. His perfection lies in seeking what benefits him and not being incapable of it. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿If you do good, you do good to your own selves﴾ [al-Isra': 7], and He said: ﴿And whatever good you spend, it will be repaid to you, and you will not be wronged﴾ [al-Baqarah: 272].

The Exalted said, in what His Messenger (ﷺ) related from Him: "O My servants, you will never reach My benefit so as to benefit Me, and you will never reach My harm so as to harm Me. O My servants, it is only your deeds that I count for you, then I repay you for them. So whoever finds good, let him praise Allah, and whoever finds other than that, let him blame none but himself."

So the created being does not, in the first intention, seek your benefit; rather, he seeks his own benefit through you.

As for the Lord, exalted is He, He wills your benefit, not His benefit from you, and that is pure benefit for you, free of any harm, unlike the created being's intention of benefiting you, for that may contain harm to you, even if only through bearing his obligation.

So reflect on this, for keeping it in view prevents you from hoping in a created being, or dealing with him instead of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, or seeking from him benefit or removal of harm, or attaching your heart to him. For he only wants his own benefit from you, not your pure benefit. This is the condition of all creatures with one another, and it is the condition of a child with his father, a husband with his wife, a slave with his master, and a partner with his partner. The happy one is the one who deals with them for the sake of Allah, the Exalted, not for their sake; who shows kindness to them for the sake of Allah, the Exalted; who fears Allah, the Exalted, regarding them, and does not fear them alongside Allah, the Exalted; who hopes in Allah, the Exalted, through showing kindness to them, and does not hope in them alongside Allah; and who loves them with the love of Allah, and does not love them alongside Allah, the Exalted, just as the friends of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿We feed you only for the sake of Allah's countenance; we do not want from you any reward or thanks﴾ [al-Insan: 9].
